## Settings

## Description  
Make Form-gate Hierarchy attempts to recognize common gate structures (such as inverters, and, nand gates). If found, it creates hierarchical cells of these gates.  
Add Net Label to All Wire Segments adds net labels to each segment of a wire rather than just one segment.  
Create Vector Ports controls whether to merge the bus bit terminals to a bus by selecting one of the following options: Off , by Ascending , or by Descending .  
For example, A<0> and A<1> to A<0:1> . You can choose to sort bus bits in ascending or descending order.  
Create Vector Instances controls whether to merge Vector Bit instances to a Vector instance by selecting one of the following options: Off , by Ascending , or by Descending .  
Instances from the source text view get merged to a Vector Instance only under the following conditions:  
The resulting Vector Instance bits order is controlled via the selected value.  
- The Instance is a Vector Bit instance.
- The placed master should match for all bits.
- The base name should match for all bits.
- Instance properties should match for all bits.  
Bit Format specifies the vector or bus bit notation format used in the source text. Target object's name is updated to match the tool's vector or bus bit notation. The name of objects (such as instances, terminals, and nets) from the source text matching to the specified bit format are placed.  
For Verilog sources, this filed is disabled and the current value is ignored. The [\d] notation is forced to use for the specified value. It should either be enclosed in [ ] or < > brackets or as a suffix prepended by a delimiter, otherwise the value considered as invalid and ignored.  
Valid values are <\d> , [\d] or any string ending by \d .  
For example, a format #\d matches all names like Inst123#4 . The default is [\d] means any name like Inst123[4] is considered as a bit and changed to the tool's default bit notation. That is Inst123<4> .  
Power recognizes the nets as power net.  
Ground recognizes the nets as ground net.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
| Settings         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Nets Connections | Create Virtual Terms as defines the virtual terminals found in the source text view are created in target schematic by selecting one of the following options: ◦ Virtual : Terminals from the source text view that have connection definition on them are not created in target schematic, instead the connection definition is copied to the corresponding net ◦ Physical : Terminals from the source text view that have connection definition on them are created in target schematic as regular terminals. ◦ Physical with Virtual : Terminals from the source text view that have connection definition on them are not copied as is (with the connection definition) to the target schematic. Connect by Name creates connections between nets by name for Selected nets, All nets, or None of the nets. Net Names is the list of patterns to match for net names when you choose Selected with Connect by Name . For example, select global nets, such as power and ground, to eliminate nets that connect to a large number of devices. Invalid patterns are ignored. Match By : Select the pattern syntax used in the Net Names text field. Valid values are Wildcard and RegExp . Case Sensitive : Controls the case sensitivity for net names matching patterns. |

## 6. Click OK .  
The system imports the text and creates the designated views.

## Generating Device Mapping File  
To create appropriate instances for netlist devices, an XML formatted device mapping file is required. The device mapping file is used mainly for determining the master cellview that should be used for instances, order of ports, and the correct instance property names and values, according to the master's CDF data.  
The $SUB syntax is now supported in the CDL format for import netlist flow.  
<!-- image -->  
To create a mapping file from a selected library, which can then be edited with additional required data:  
1. On the Import Text dialog box, click generate to open the Generate Device Mapping File dialog box, as illustrated in the following figure.  
<!-- image -->  
(Clicking Generate on the Generate Schematic from Text dialog box also opens the same Generate Device Mapping File dialog box).  
2. Browse to select the Reference Libraries and the Generated File Path where the file resides. Enter the View Search List from which to generate the mapping data (the default is symbol ), and the Cell Name , where cell name matching allows wildcard characters.
3. Specify which SimInfo section to be used for device mapping file template generation (the default is hspiceD ).
4. (Optional) Select Overwrite to overwrite any existing mapping file.
5. Click Generate to generate the file. See Device Mapping File Format.

## Device Mapping File Format  
The device mapping file contains the following simple xml format:  
```
<file-format version="1.0" name="synopsysDeviceMappingFile" > <deviceMappings><deviceMapping> <devType>devType</devType> <cellType>cellType</cellType> <models>modelname ...</models> <regModels>regModels</regModels> <portProp>portProp</portProp> <ports><{>p1<[portProp]> ...<}> <{>p2<[portProp]> ...<}> ...</ports> <portDefaultNets>pr1(n1) pr2(n2) ...</portDefaultNets > <propMatching>p1=v1 p2=v2 ...</propMatching> <lcv>libname/cellname/viewname</lcv>
```  
<!-- image -->  
```
<propMapping>p1<(v1, v2, ...)>=mp1<(mv1, mv2, ...)></propMapping> <stringParameters>p1[(p1v1, p2v2, ...)] p2(p2v1, p2v2, ...) ... <stringParameters> <appProps>appProps</appProps> </deviceMapping> ... </deviceMappings> </file-format>
```  
Each deviceMapping record can contain the following tags:  
- devType
- cellType
- models
- regModels
- portProp
- ports
- portDefaultNets
- propMatching
- lcv
- propMapping
- stringParameters
- appProps  
All tags are optional except <devType> and <lcv> . Note that only the cell part of the lcv field is required; the library and view names can be absent, which indicate that the libSearchList and viewSearchList property values are used to search for a cellview with the given cell name.  
The values of the following tags are examined for determining the correct lcv to be used for a device: devType , cellType , models , ports , and propMatching . All the other fields are used to correctly map the device/instance parameter names and to create correct instance connections.  
To find a matching lcv , the values of these tags are examined in the following order: devType , cellType , models , ports , propMatching . Matching to a device/instance declaration is done in the following steps, where each step does its filtering among the records which have been filtered after the previous steps:  
<!-- image -->  
1. Find the records having the devType of the given device.
2. Find those records which contain in their models field the name of the model specified in the device declaration. If no model has been specified in the device declaration or no matching record has been found, searching for a record with an empty model field, which is considered as a default mapping for that device type, is done.
3. For active elements for which the N or P type has been recognized from the netlist file, using the model card information or checking the model name against the N or P type patterns and a record with an empty model name has been found only, check also that the found cell's cellType matches the model type.
4. Check among the found records for those which have a ports field with port number corresponding to the number of nets in the device declaration.
5. For each record matching the preceding conditions, as the final matched record is considered the first one having propMatching conditions to which the parameters in the device declaration match.  
If no matching device mapping is found for the device declaration, the device is considered as unbound. For instances for which no mapping is found the module name specified in the instance declaration is considered as a name for a master cell.  
If a matching mapping record is found for an instance or a device, that instance is created with a master cellview specified in the lcv field. Instance connections are done according to the ports and portDefaultNets fields' values and the instance properties' creation is done according to the propMapping field's value. The ports with names given in the ports field are by order connected to given in the device declaration nets. The remaining ports are connected according to the connections specified in the defaultPortNets field.  
For correct instance property creation, the propMapping field's value is used in the following way: parameters given in the device declaration for which the mapping data exists in the propMapping field, are mapped according to the specified mapped name and values. Note that for CDL devices, the names of the parameters which are netlisted with a proceeding $ sign, should be specified in the device mapping file with $ sign as well, for example: a capacitor's $w parameter following data can be specified in the propMapping and propMatching tags correspondingly as $W=w and $w>2u .

## devType  
devType for devices is the device name prefix for SPICE (R, C, L, W, U, and so on) and is the primitive name for Verilog (tranif0, tranif1, nand, and so on). For module/ subckt instantiations, devType should be X for SPICE and module for Verilog. Subckt instantiations, which are actually subckt models, can be mapped using the X<devType> prefix, for example XM , XC , and so on. This allows to map the subckt model instantiations, with the X<device\_prefix> instance name prefix, the same way as the real device instantiations.  
<!-- image -->  
The devType tag can contain more than one device type, to support identical mapping for same type devices and subcircuit models, for example: M XM ' and R XR .

## cellType  
cellType is used for specifying the cellType of the mapped device. For active elements, it should indicate whether the device is of N or P type. Valid values for active elements are NMOS and PMOS (for MOSFET devices), NJFET and PJFET (for JFET devices), and NPN and PNP (for BJT devices). For all other SPICE devices, the cellType should be the same as the devType .  
The cellType tag is used mainly for schematic generation purposes. For active elements, cellType is used to correctly map the devices recognized to be of N or P type. The N or P type is recognized from the model card if it exists. Otherwise if no model card exists, or the device instantiated a subckt model, the N or P type is recognized by matching the model name with a pattern. The pattern checks for the first symbol of the model/subkct name to see if it is N or P , if it is not then checks which of the N and P symbols appears more times in the name.

## models  
models contains the model names that can be specified in the device declarations. Note that this field can be empty indicating that the current lcv is the default one for the specified device type, and in case if no model name is specified in the device declaration or no lcv mapping is found for the specified model, the given default lcv is used.  
For MOSFET, JFET, and BJT devices which can be of N or P type, different default mappings can be specified for N and P type elements. For this purpose, one of the following can be specified as the model name: nmos, pmos, njfet, pjfet, npn, pnp.  
For module/subckt instantiations, models should contain the module/subckt name.

## Examples  
<deviceMapping> <devType>M </devType> <models>MM1 MM2</models> <lcv>myLib/nmos/symbol</lcv> <deviceMapping>  
<deviceMapping> <devType>M</devType> <models>pmos</models> <lcv>myLib/pmos1/symbol</lcv> <deviceMapping>  
<deviceMapping>  
```
<devType>M</devType> <models> </models> <lcv>myLib/nmos2/symbol</lcv> <deviceMapping> <deviceMapping> <devType>X</devType> <models>cell1</models> <lcv>myLib/mycell/symbol</lcv> <deviceMapping>
```  
According to the previously mentioned device mapping records, the following device declarations are mapped to the following cells:  
```
.model MM1 nmos .model MM3 pmos .model MM4 nmos M1 n1 n2 n3 MM1 1 2 // maps to myLib/nmos/symbol M3 n1 n2 n3 MM3 1 2 // myLib/pmos1/symbol M4 n1 n2 n3 MM4 1 2 // myLib/nmos2/symbol as there is no mapping declared for MM4 M5 n1 n2 n3 MM5 1 2 // myLib/nmos2/symbol as there is no mapping declared for MM5 X1 n1 n2 n3 cell1  // myLib/mycell/symbol X2 n1 n2 n3 cell2  // is not mapped, libSearchList and viewSearchList properties are used to find a cell with name cell2
```

## regModels  
<regModels> is used for adding regular expressions to match model names. The regular expression matching has lower priority than the exact model name matching which is done by the <models> tag. If a model name parsed matched both <models> and <regModels> tags, the <models> tag is honored if the ports and parameters matched.  
You can define multiple patterns in a <regModels> </regModels> tag pair by separating each pattern using a space character. The regular expression pattern model matching is supported in both the legacy parser flow (TN library) and the new common parser flow (GNDB) for SPICE/CDL format. If a device mapping section in the device mapping file both have <models> and <regModels> tags, only the <regModels> tag is honored.

## portProp  
portProp is the name of the property, which is used for the PCells with generated number of ports. For example, for W, U, and S devices, the number of ports is not fixed and if a PCell is used as the master, the ports are generated according to property value like portnumber . And because the device declaration contains no such parameter, its value should be calculated from the number of net names given in the device declaration and certain port list pattern given in ports .  
<!-- image -->

## ports  
ports contains the list of ports to which the nets given in the device declaration should be connected by order.

## Note that:  
- The connected ports that should be connected to a net are given as a list. The port names in the i-th list are connected to the net which corresponds to the net on i-th position in the device declaration, for example, for PCells with a variable number of ports, if you want MOSFETs with 3 nodes to connect to a master with 4 terminals, specify the following port list meaning that the last net is connected both to ports S and B: G D {S B} .
- If the net given in some positions in the device declaration should not be connected to any net, an empty list can be specified instead of the port name, for example: for a MOSFET device, the list of ports can contain the following: {} G D S , meaning that the first name given in the device declaration should not be connected to any port, and the remaining 3 nets should be connected to G, D, and S ports correspondingly.
- Given port names can be either the names of existing ports in the cellview or the names of virtual terminals to which the nets from the device declaration should be connected. So any port name given in the list is considered as a terminal name, if such exists in the design, otherwise it is considered as a virtual terminal name to which the given net should be assigned. Use the teParseExtraTermsAsVirtual Tcl preference to decide whether extra port names should be considered as virtual terminals.
- For PCells, the ports of which are generated depending on property values (given in the portProp field), port names can be specified as a port name prefix followed by a bracket with the portProp name inside, for example, {in[n]} {refin} {out[n]} {refout} for w element. This indicates that the port names should be generated with the given prefix appended with indexes from 1 to n . Note that the value of n is actually calculated from the number of nets given in the device declarations. For example, for the preceding W element port pattern, the number of nets should be 2n+2 and if the device declaration contains 6 nets, n is calculated as 2, so the generated port names should be in1 in2 refin out1 out2 refout .
- If the ports field is empty, the portOrder/termOrder of the device is used for instterm connection. (If those properties are also empty, the instance remains unconnected).

## portDefaultNets  
portDefaultNets defines the default connections for ports with the following format: pr1(n1) pr2(n2) , where pr i is the port name, and n i is the net that should connect to it if no other connection is specified for the port in the ports field.  
For CDL netlists, this portDefaultNets tag can contain also port connections in the following format: pi($param) , which indicates that p i port should be connected to the net the name of which is given as a value of $param parameter. Note that port-to-parameter connections are considered as overriding for those made according to the ports field. This means that if the ports field contains p1 p2 p3 p4 for a BJT element, and the portDefaultNets field contains value p4($SUB) , port p4 is connected to the net the names of which is specified as a value of $SUB parameter in the BJT device declaration.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->

## propMatching  
To have the specified in the device mapping record lcv to be used as the master for the given device, propMatching defines the conditions to which the parameter values in the instance declaration should match.  
propMatching can contain a set of conditions on more than one parameter represented as expressions with equal ( == ), not equal ( != ), less ( < ), greater ( > ), less or equal ( <= ), and greater or equal ( >= ) operators. propMatching can also indicate matching by parameter existence or absence.  
Note that more than one propMatching tag can be given in a device mapping record. To have matching with the case when a particular parameter is given in the device declaration, the parameter name should be specified in propMatching , and to indicate the opposite (the parameter is not given in the device declaration), a ! sign should be set before the parameter name. For example: w<2u , l>4u , or !CONVOLUTION ! FBASE !FMAX !RS which indicates that the specified master should be chosen only for linear transistors, which exclude the usage of this cellview as the master for frequency dependent and skin effect resistors.

## lcv  
lcv contains the library, cell, and view names (separated by slashes) of the master cellview that should be used as a master for the device declaration which matches the data of all the previous fields. Note that if the library or view name is empty, libSearchList and viewSearchList values are used instead to search a given cell name in the listed libraries.

## propMapping  
propMapping contains the mapping of hspice parameter names and their values to corresponding parameter names and values for the given cell's CDF data. For example:  
- tranfun(SIN,PU)=srcType(SINE,PULSE) means that SPICE parameter tranfun is mapped to CDF parameter srcType and its values SIN and PU are mapped correspondingly to values SINE and PULSE .
- R=res means that the R value of the SPICE device is saved in RES parameter of the OA instance.

## stringParameters  
stringParameters contains the mapped names of string and enumeration type parameters for a given device.  
The stringParameters tag is used for correct replacing of identifier names representing parameter names with lineage("param\_name") expression in the instance parameter values. This is needed for correct schematic generation to make parameter evaluation look for the parameter value in upper levels of the hierarchy.  
For string parameters, only the names should be listed, while for enumerated parameters, the tag can contain the parameter name followed by the supported enumeration values in brackets separated by commas, so that other string values passed to this parameter are considered as parameter names.  
Also, non-string parameters that can have some string keyword values should be listed in this stringParameters tag. For example, keyword infinity for capacitor device's parameter C : C(infinity) .

## appProps  
appProps contains the name of parameters which should be created in OA as instance properties if specified in the device declaration, even if they are not valid parameters according to the SPICE documentation, does not exist in the CDF and are not specified in the propMapping field.

## Device Mapping File Examples  
The following lines show examples of deviceMapping records.  
```
<deviceMappings> <!-mapping Sinusoidal voltage sources to the vsin cellview of analoglib . --> <deviceMapping> <devType> V </devType> <model> </model> <portProp></portProp> <ports> PLUS MINUS </ports> <propMatching> tranfun=sin </propMatching> <lcv> analogLib vsin symbol </lcv> <propMapping> tranfun(SIN)=srcType(Sine) dc=vdc acmag=acm acphase=acPhase vo=vo va=va td=td freq=freq q=q j=j </propMapping> <appProps>z</appProps> </deviceMapping> <!-mapping FET transistors (with 3 ports) with models named M1 and M2 to analoglib nmos (which is 3-port device with virtual terminal p_bulk),
```  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
```
and the model names M1 and M2 are mapped as nmos1 and nmos2. The bulk is connected to the same net as the source. --> <deviceMapping> <devType> M </devType> <model> M1 M2</model> <portProp></portProp> <ports> {G} {D} {S p_bulk} </ports> <propMatching> </propMatching> <lcv> analogLib nmos hspice </lcv> <propMapping>vds=Vds vgs=Vgs vbs=Vbs mname(M1,M2)=model(nmos1, nmos2) </propMapping> <appProps>a b</appProps> </deviceMapping> <!-mapping FET transistors (with 4 ports) with models named M3 and M4 to analoglib nmos (which is 3-port device and has a virtual terminal p_bulk), and the model names M3 and M4 are mapped as nmos3 and nmos4. The bulk is connected to the same net as the source. --> <deviceMapping> <devType> M </devType> <model> M3 M4</model> <portProp></portProp> <ports> {G} {D} {S} {p_bulk} </ports> <propMatching> </propMatching> <lcv> analogLib nmos hspice </lcv> <propMapping>vds=Vds vgs=Vgs vbs=Vbs l=l w=w mname(M3,M4)=model(nmos3, nmos4) </propMapping> <appProps>a b</appProps> </deviceMapping> <!-mapping High voltage FET transistors with models named HVP1 and HVP2 to analoglib nmos4v, and the model names HVP1 and HVP2 are mapped as nmos1 and nmos2. --> <deviceMapping> <devType> M </devType> <model> HVP1 HVP2</model> <portProp></portProp> <ports> {G} {D} {S} {B} </ports> <propMatching> </propMatching> <lcv> analogLib pmos4hv symbol </lcv> <propMapping>vds=Vds vgs=Vgs vbs=Vbs mname(HVP1, HVP2)=model(pmos1hv, pmos2hv) </propMapping> <appProps>a b</appProps> </deviceMapping> <!-mapping skin effect resistor to the myLib skin_effect_res symbol of myLib library,--> <deviceMapping> <devType> R </devType> <model> </model>
```  
<!-- image -->  
```
<portProp></portProp> <ports> {PLUS} {MINUS}</ports> <propMatching> rs </propMatching> <lcv> myLib skin_effect_res symbol </lcv> <propMapping> rs=RS </propMapping> <appProps></appProps> </deviceMapping> <!-mapping pdif resistor to the myLib resPdif symbol --> <deviceMapping> <devType> R </devType> <model>pdifres pdres </model> <portProp></portProp> <ports> {PLUS} {MINUS}</ports> <propMatching> </propMatching> <lcv> myLib resPdif symbol </lcv> <propMapping> r=res mname=modelName </propMapping> <appProps></appProps> </deviceMapping> <!-mapping resistor with TC1>3 to the analogLib res symbol and settingmodelname to nwelRes --> <deviceMapping> <devType> R </devType> <model> </model> <portProp></portProp> <ports> {PLUS} {MINUS}</ports> <propMatching> TC1>3 </propMatching> <lcv> analogLib res symbol </lcv> <propMapping> r=res </propMapping> <propDefaults> modelName(nwelRes) </propDefaults> <appProps></appProps> </deviceMapping> <!-mapping frequency dependent resistor to the myLib resFreq symbol --> <deviceMapping> <devType> R </devType> <model> </model> <portProp></portProp> <ports> {PLUS} {MINUS}</ports> <propMatching> CONVOLUTION </propMatching> <lcv> myLib resFreq symbol </lcv> <propMapping> rs=RS </propMapping> <appProps></appProps> </deviceMapping> <!-mapping W device to analogLib mtline device. This is an example with the portProp usage, when the number of ports is variable. --> <deviceMapping> <devType> W </devType> <model> </model> <portProp>n</portProp>
```  
```
<ports> {in[n]} {refin} {out[n]} {refout}</ports> <lcv> myLib skin_effect_res symbol </lcv> <propMapping>… </propMapping> <appProps></appProps> </deviceMapping> </deviceMappings>
```

## Importing Design Netlist Data for Schematic Generation  
You can import design netlist data to generate schematics without creating text views. Available text netlist formats include SPICE, CDL, and Verilog. You can optionally generate symbol views while importing netlist text.  
Compressed files that are supported by the Linux zcat command are supported by this flow. Compressed file support can also be enhanced using the db::showGenerateSchematicsFromText::decompressFiles procedure.  
To import design data for schematic generation:  
1. From the Home or Console tab, choose File>Import> Schematic from Netlist to open the Generate Schematics from Text dialog box.
2. On the Main tab, enter settings as described in Table33.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
| Settings       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Input          | Language is the behavioral modeling language you specify from the list: SPICE , CDL , Verilog , Verilog-A , Verilog-AMS , SystemVerilog , or VHDL . Netlist Files specifies the source netlist for this import process. Browse to select the file. Multiple files can also be selected. Top Cell Name works for CDL and SPICE formats only. Enter the name of a cell where top-level SPICE/CDL design data should be put. A name based off the imported file name is generated by default. Import Modules lets you list module names or specify the name pattern for the modules you wish to import. Match Type can be Exact , Reg Expr , or Wildcard . Exclude Modules lets you list module names or specify the name pattern for the modules you wish to exclude from the import when |
| Device Mapping | Device Map File works for SPICE, CDL, and Verilog formats only. You can click any of the following buttons: ◦ Device Mapping File for resolving instance masters to designate the required device mapping source (to resolve instance masters to reference libraries) from a file. ◦ Generate to create the device map file from a reference library. See Generating Device Mapping File. Click Edit Mapping File to open the selected mapping file in a text editor for adding or modifying the mapping information. Click Default to load the sample provided with the installation hierarchy. This file can also be copied and edited to address any missing information. The default mapping file maps all devices to analogLib library cells.                                      |
| Output         | Library specifies the destination library for this import operation, which you choose from the list. Click Create Library to open the New Library dialog box and create a new output library. View Name shows the view name of the schematic view that is generated. Overwrite specifies how the import process treats imported cellViews that conflict with existing cellViews. Never (the default) means that the existing cellView remains intact (no copy is created). Always means that existing cellViews are overwritten.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |  
Table 33 Generate Schematics From Text Settings (Main tab)  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
| Settings   | Description                                                                                                   |
|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|            | Create Port Order controls whether the portOrder property should be created in the generated schematic views. |
|            | Check After Creation runs ERC/SRC checks after schematic creation.                                            |
|            | Evaluate Callbacks enables instance parameter callback evaluation during schematic generation.                |
## Settings

## Description  
Store Views by File Extension stores imported netlist with default view name specified with preference dbImportText<Language>ViewName . So, the Tcl preferences are dbImportTextVerilogViewName for Verilog, dbImportTextVerilogAMSViewName Verilog AMS, and dbImportTextSystemVerilogViewName for Syntem Verilog.  
You can specify Verilog (*.v), Verilog-AMS (*.vams), and System-Verilog (*.sv) netlist files in the Netlist Files box to import them simultaneously.  
This option appears when Language is set to Verilog , Verilog-AMS , or SystemVerilog .  
When this option is enabled, the View Name option is disabled. The tool recognizes file format by file extension defined with the preference dbImportText<Langugage>FileExtensions . So, the Tcl Preferences are dbImportTextVerilogFileExtensions for *.v, dbImportTextVerilogAMSFileExtensions for *.vams, and dbImportTextSystemVerilogFileExtensions for *.sv.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
3. On the Options tab, enter settings as described in Table34.  
<!-- image -->  
Table 34 Generate Schematics From Text Settings (Options Tab)

Make Form-gate Hierarchy attempts to recognize common gate structures (such as inverters, and, nand gates). If found, it creates hierarchical cells of these gates.

Create Vector Ports controls whether to merge the bus bit terminals to a bus by selecting one of the following options: Off , by Ascending , or by Descending .  
For example, A<0> and A<1> to A<0:1> . You can choose to sort bus bits in ascending or descending order.  
Create Vector Instances controls whether to merge Vector Bit instances to a Vector instance by selecting one of the following options: Off , by Ascending , or by Descending .  
Instances from the source text view get merged to a Vector Instance only under the following conditions:  
The resulting Vector Instance bits order is controlled via the selected value.  
- The Instance is a Vector Bit instance.
- The placed master should match for all bits.
- The base name should match for all bits.

For Verilog sources, this filed is disabled and the current value is ignored. The [\d] notation is forced to use for the specified value. It should either be enclosed in [ ] or < > brackets or as a suffix prepended by a delimiter, otherwise the value considered as invalid and ignored.  
Valid values are <\d> , [\d] or any string ending by \d .  
For example, a format #\d matches all names like Inst123#4 . The default is [\d] means any name like Inst123[4] is considered as a bit and changed to the tool's default bit notation. That is Inst123<4> .

Use Specified Mapping allows you to specify manually the terminal names to be created as virtual.  
Click Edit to open the Term Mapping dialog box and enter terminal name to definition name mapping (the default net name mapping entries); for example, terminal name > (connection definition, default net name). These are the parameters required for creating a connection definition for a terminal.  
<!-- image -->  
On import, the name of any terminal found in the subcircuit declaration is matched against the terminal names in the specified mapping table. If the mapping table has an entry for the terminal being looked up, it is created as virtual using the specified definition and default net name.  
The name matching is done according to the netlist type. If the netlist is case-insensitive, name matching is done case-insensitively and the connection definition is created with the specified parameter names in lower case. If the netlist is case-sensitive, name matching is done case-sensitively and the connection definition is created as specified by the user.  
Use Automatic Mapping if Unspecified allows for the automatic determination/recognition of the terminals to be created as virtual, using the specified reference view list. If this option is selected (and Use Specified Mapping is unselected), the subcircuit terminal names are compared with the terminal names in the Reference Views (the first view on the list is considered first and each successive view is checked only if the preceding view does not exist). If the netlist contains a terminal that is not found in the Reference Views text field, it is created as virtual using the terminal name followed by bang (!) as the connection definition and the default net name. For example, for terminal vdd that is on the netlist but not in the Reference Views , a connection definition is created using the default mapping (vdd!, vdd!).  
If both Use Specified Mapping and Use Automatic Mapping if Unspecified are selected, to determine whether or not to create a terminal as virtual, its name is first looked up in the user-specified mapping table. If it is not found, automatic mapping is tried next.

| Include Files | Specifies whether all include files should be parsed or ignored. The options are: ◦ Parse : Parses the include files and creates the cells for modules found in the include files. Include statements are not added to any module. For Verilog, effective directives are calculated and included for each module. ◦ Ignore : The include files are parsed, but the modules declared inside the include files are not created. Include statements are not added to the modules. For Verilog, effective directives are calculated and included for each module. For SPICE and CDL, you can use the Except rows to create multiple Parse / Ignore exceptions to the All files directive. Click to add an Except row under the current row, or to delete the current row. Match type for the exception can be Exact , Reg Expr , or Wildcard (the default). Exceptions are prioritized such that the lowermost condition is checked first; if there is no match, then the next condition up the list is checked, and so on. In other words, lower conditions have higher priority. Default exceptions are: ◦ Include files with extensions .dspf , .gz , .gzip , .enc and .spf . ◦ Ignore files with extensions .data , .ic , .lib , and .vec . |

## Importing Design Data in EDIF 200 Format  
EDIF is a common schematic format that is generated by many electronic CAD tools. Import design data as EDIF200 when you want to translate data files from an Electronic Design Interchange Format (EDIF) schematic to the Custom Compiler database.

metadata.Header 2: Using the Import EDIF200 Dialog Box

content:
## Using the Import EDIF200 Dialog Box  
To import design data as EDIF200:  
1. From the Home or Console tab, choose File>Import>EDIF200 to open the Import EDIF200 dialog box.
2. Enter settings as described in Table36.  
Figure 20 Import EDIF200 Dialog Box: General Options  
<!-- image -->  
| Settings   | Description                                                                        |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Input File | The schematic or netlist input design file. Note: Custom Compiler does not support |
|            | importing EDIF files that define multipage schematics.                             |

<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
| Settings            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|---------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Output Library Name | The target design library. The EDIF format defines library names of cellviews being imported. If Output Library Name is not specified, Custom Compiler tries to create required libraries with names defined in EDIF file. The EDIF file could specify more than one library. If the Output Library Name is specified, all cellviews are created in the specified library regardless of their libNames defined in the EDIF file. In the case of conflicting cell names (for example, if the library being used already has such a cell), the tool renames the cell name using the format <LibNameFromEDIF>_cellName. |
| Top Cell Name       | The top cell of the design to be translated. The EDIF file can contain many hierarchies, for example A > B > C and A1 > B1 > C1. If Top Cell Name is not specified, both hierarchies (6 cells) are imported. If, however, Top Cell Name is specified as A1, only the A1 > B1 > C1 hierarchy is imported. If Top Cell Name is specified as a mid-level cell name, such as B, Custom Compiler imports only the hierarchy starting from that mid-level cell, such as B > C.                                                                                                                                             |  
3. On the General tab (Figure20), enter settings as described in Table37.

| Overwrite                 | Overwrites existing cell views after import. On by default.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Create symbols only       | Imports only symbol views from the importing file, discarding everything else. This option can be used with Output Library Name to build a symbols library of the file being imported.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| PreParse results log file | If a file path is defined, Custom Compiler does not import the specified EDIF file, but instead preparses it to collect the Library/Cell/View information of cellviews defined in the EDIF file. The complete list of Libraries/Cells/Views is output to the log file specified by the PreParse results log file option.                                          |
| CDF files directory       | The path to the directory in which to search a CDF file for a cell. If the EDIF file being imported has a cell with a cdfData property of string type defined, Custom Compiler tries to find a file of the name specified by this property in the directory specified by this option. If found, all parameters defined in that CDF file are appended to the cell. |  
<!-- image -->  
4. On the Names case tab (Figure21), enter settings as described in Table38. This dialog box controls the capitalization (case) of object names imported from the EDIF file.

Tcl preference: dbEDIFImportCustomSchematicDBUPerUU                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Data source                            | Specifies vendor-specific data semantics. Options are Composer (the default) or ViewDraw . Custom Compiler uses this option to correctly map array instance names, sub-bus net names and some parameter names/values. For example, if Data source is set to ViewDraw and a schematic defined in the EDIF file has a net name MyNet1, Custom Compiler tries to find a bus net with base name MyNet. If found, and the found bus includes bit ％1, then the net name MyNet1 is mapped to MyNet<1>. This option is also used to set the array names' braces used in the source EDIF file. If set to ViewDraw , square brackets [] are treated as array names; otherwise, angle brackets <> are treated as array names. |

## 6. Click OK .  
The system imports the file and creates the designated views.

## Export  
This chapter describes how to export design and library data using the Custom Compiler Console. The data can be exported to ICCompiler, GDSII Stream, OASIS, LEF, DEF, Liberty File, and netlist formats. To protect the proprietary information stored in your Tcl scripts, you can export it in bytecode format.  
- Exporting Design Data in GDSII Stream Format
- Exporting Design Data in OASIS Format
- Exporting Design Data in Library Exchange Format (LEF)
- Exporting Design Data in Design Exchange Format (DEF)
- Exporting Design Data in Liberty Library File Format
- Exporting Design Data in Netlist Format

## Note:  
Exporting Designs and Libraries to the IC Compiler Tool is covered in the Custom Compiler and IC Compiler Co-Design Assistant User Guide .  
To export technology data instead of design data, use the Technology Manager Tool.

## Settings

## Description  
Color Locks specifies which mapping lines in the layer mapping file are used to map shapes with a mask color attribute.

## Options for Color Locks are:  
A color specification is present in the layer mapping file if the data type number is followed by the keyword color with a colon (:) and a color name. Optionally, this entry can be followed by one of the keywords locked or unlocked . locked refers to the anchor bit in the color value for the shape.  
- Ignore : All colored shapes are mapped with the line that has neither keyword.
- Full : Mapping is compatible with Cadence® Virtuoso®, with the following behavior: The keyword colorAnnotate after the color specification in the layer map is used to ignore a whole line of layer mapping during GDSII Stream export and the same mapping line is handled during import.
- Strict : Anchor bit is used to select either locked or unlocked from the layer map.
- Honor : (default) Mapping is compatible with Cadence® Virtuoso®, with the following behavior: When the layer map does not have a color mapping rule in to match color shapes, the Custom Compiler tool tries to match the mapping rule without a color specified.  
Example:  
- DisableColor : Layer mapping lines with a color attribute in the layer mapping file are ignored. Any shape with color does not map those mapping lines with color attributes. Only mapping lines without a color attribute is used for layer mapping.  
M1 drawing 3 0  
M1 drawing 3 12 color:red unlocked  
M1 drawing 3 11 color:red locked

- Lock Only : The shapes of the colored layer that are not colored or are not locked, are filtered out during export.  
dbExportStreamShowLockOnly preference to true . The default setting is false .  
PCell options control conversion of PCells into their geometry. The default is Keep .  
The Flatten option flattens PCells, editable PCells, and MCells, obeying the hierarchy limit.  
The None option means no conversion.  
The Keep option preserves the information of PCells, editable PCells, MCells, and MPP in the GDS stream file, so that they can be restored during import using Import > Stream > Options > Restore PCells . Abutment information is stored in a side file and can also be restored during import.

Cell Name Prefix specifies the string prefixed to every structure name written in the Stream file. The GUI validates that the string entered is a legal CDBA scalar name, and that it also contains no spaces. If left empty, no option is used. Note that this option does not exist in oa2strm .  
Cell Name Suffix specifies the string suffixed to every structure name written in the Stream file. The GUI validates that the string entered is a legal CDBA scalar name, and that it also contains no spaces. If left empty, no option is used. Note that this option does not exist in oa2strm .  
Ignore Top Cells Prefix and Suffix Specifies whether top cells listed in Main > Input > Top Cell should be added with a prefix or suffix. Default is No.  
Ignore Cells Prefix and Suffix Ignores the prefixes and suffixes of the cells listed in this field. Use blank space to separate cells.  
Hierarchy Depth is the number of hierarchy levels to translate. Default is 256.

| Settings   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Output     | Reference specifies the output reference mapping file. Specify a path to the file in the text box. This file is important when you export a GDSII file from Custom Compiler, run IC Validator DRC or LVS, and then cross-probe or highlight these violations to the Custom Compiler Layout Editor. In this flow, ICV reports violations with respect to the GDSII library/cell object context, but Custom Compiler must identify and probe the corresponding objects and coordinates in the OpenAccess lib/cell/view context. This reference mapping file stores the mapping relationship between the OpenAccess objects, (such as vias, PCells, lib/cell/view hierarchy, and so on) and their equivalent GDSII objects. Having this file ensures that you can cross-probe violations from a GDSII-based ICV run into Custom Compiler LE; this is the supported and recommended flow. metadata.Header 2: Exporting Design Data in OASIS Format

content:
## Exporting Design Data in OASIS Format  
To export design data in OASIS format:  
1. Perform any one of the following to open the Export OASIS dialog box:
- From the Home tab, choose File > Export > OASIS .
- From the toolbar in the Layout Editor, choose Design > Export OASIS  
Figure 28 Export OASIS Dialog Box: Main Tab  
<!-- image -->  
2. On the Main tab, enter settings as described in Table46.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->

## Settings  
Output Description Merge CellViews is the field you use to specify the list of cell views to export, to be merged to the top cellview. The cellviews are separated with spaces. Each cellview is specified using the following format: libName/cellName/viewName.  
Preference: dbExportOasisMergeCellviews  
To generate the list of cellviews, click the browse button. The Export Oasis Merge Cellviews Browser dialog box opens. Select the cell views to merge, and click OK .  
<!-- image -->  
Run Directory is the directory you browse to select, or a new directory you create by entering its name. The default is the current directory.  
OASIS File is the OASIS file you browse to select and use. Click the folder icon to open the Select File dialog box.  
To find OASIS files more quickly, select the *.oas *.oasis *.OAS *.OASIS filter in the Files of type box.  
<!-- image -->  
Multiple Files : Creates an OASIS file for each cell defined in the Top Cell box in the Input section simultaneously.  
Tcl preference: dbExportOasisMultipleFiles  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
| Settings     | Description                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Notification | Display Notification When Complete When selected, the Export OASIS Results dialog box appears after export. Click View Logs to see the log file, or OK to exit the dialog box. |
| Basic        | Invoke Batch Mode When selected (the default), runs exportOasis integrated with the Custom Compiler tool. Uncheck this option to run as a standalone utility.                  |  
3. Click the Options tab in the Export OASIS dialog box (Figure29).
4. On the Options tab, enter settings as described in Table47.  
Figure 29 Export OASIS Dialog Box: Options Tab  
<!-- image -->  
Table 47 Export OASIS Settings (Options Tab)  
## Settings  
General

## Description  
Apply Repetition exports repeated instances, shapes, and text in --repetition mode so that they occupy less disk space. Off by default.  
Expand Arrays to Instances specifies whether to convert arrays to instances. Off by default.  
Convert All Paths to Polygons exports paths as a polygon describing the complete shape boundary rather than as a path object. Off by default.  
Convert Ellipses to Circles exports the conversion from circles to polygons. If this option is disabled, circles remain circles during export. Off by default.  
Export Text Displays controls translation of textDisplay objects. On by default.  
Export Blockages controls export of blockage objects. Default is to export blockage objects (on).  
Export Reference Library Cells controls translation and output of cells referenced from a library other than the one specified by the Library argument. Default is that these cells are translated.  
Snap Vertices to Mfg Grid specifies whether the translator should snap the object vertices to manufacturing grid during export. Off by default.  
Keep Vias specifies whether the translator should write via information into the .pcell file. On by default.  
Flatten Standard Vias specifies whether the translator should convert standard vias into their geometry. Off by default.  
Keep Full Cell Name specifies whether to keep the full name of the cells. When turned off, cell names are shortened during export. Off by default.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
| Settings   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|            | Duplicate Cell specifies what the translator should do during export: ◦ Append with Number : (default) Append the duplicate cell name with a sequence number. ◦ Append with Library Name : Append the duplicate cell name with a source library name. ◦ Skip Duplicate : Skips the duplicate cell name when the same cell name is found during export stream. After duplicating the cell name, the tool appends the suffix with the view name if the view name is not a layout. However, if the cell name still duplicates even after appending the suffix with the view name, the Duplicate Cell option specifies that the translator should append the duplicate cell name with a sequence number during export. |
## Settings

## Description  
Color Locks specifies which mapping lines in the layer mapping file are used to map shapes with a mask color attribute.

## Options for Color Locks are:  
A color specification is present in the layer mapping file if the data type number is followed by the keyword color with a colon (:) and a color name. Optionally, this entry can be followed by one of the keywords locked or unlocked . locked refers to the anchor bit in the color value for the shape.  
- Ignore : All colored shapes are mapped with the line that has neither keyword.
- Full : Mapping is compatible with Cadence® Virtuoso®, with the following behavior: The keyword colorAnnotate after the color specification in the layer map is used to ignore a whole line of layer mapping during GDSII Stream export and the same mapping line is handled during import.
- Strict : Anchor bit is used to select either locked or unlocked from the layer map.
- Honor : (default) Mapping is compatible with Cadence® Virtuoso®, with the following behavior: When the layer map does not have a color mapping rule in to match color shapes, the Custom Compiler tool tries to match the mapping rule without a color specified.

## Example:  
- DisableColor : Layer mapping lines with a color attribute in the layer mapping file are ignored. Any shape with color does not map those mapping lines with color attributes. Only mapping lines without a color attribute is used for layer mapping.  
M1 drawing 3 0  
M1 drawing 3 12 color:red unlocked  
M1 drawing 3 11 color:red locked  
When the DisableColor option is set, colored/colorless shapes on M1 are mapped to 3 0.  
Lock Only is available only when you set the  
- Lock Only : The shapes of the colored layer that are not colored or are not locked, are filtered out during export.  
dbExportOasisShowLockOnly preference to true . The default setting is false .  
The PCell options control the conversion of PCells into their geometry:  
- Flatten flattens PCells.
- None means no conversion.
- Keep specifies whether the translator should output PCell information for a later import operation. On by default. Starting with the P-2019.06 release, Keep also specifies whether the translator should output abutment information provided the Tcl preference, dbExportOasisKeepAbutments , is set to true .  
<!-- image -->
## Settings

## Description  
Validation Scheme specifies the validation scheme to use. Valid values are None for no validation, CRC32 (default), or CHECKSUM32 .  
Compression Level is the level of compression used when writing the file. 0 is the lowest and 9 is the highest level of compression. Default is 0.  
Convert Names Specifies translator conversion of cell and instance name text to one of the following:  
- Lower : Lowercase
- None : (default) Do not convert names
- Upper : Uppercase  
Cell Name Prefix specifies a string that is prefixed to every structure name written in the stream file. The GUI validates that the string entered is a legal CDBA scalar name, and that it also contains no spaces. If left empty, no option is used. Note that this option does not exist in oa2strm .  
Cell Name Suffix specifies a string that is suffixed to every cell name. The GUI validates that the string entered is a legal CDBA scalar name, and that it also contains no spaces. If left empty, no option is used.  
Ignore Top Cells Prefix and Suffix Specifies whether top cells listed in Main > Input > Top Cell should be added with a prefix or suffix. Default is No.  
Ignore Cells Prefix and Suffix Ignores the prefixes and suffixes of the cells listed in this field. Use blank space to separate cells.  
Hierarchy Depth is the number of hierarchy levels to translate. Default is 20.  
Sides per Ellipse specifies the number of edges used for ellipse to polygon conversion. Default is 64.  
Note: If ellipses are not converted to polygons and the ellipses are circles and the diameters are even, they are exported as circles instead of polygons in the OASIS file. Cell/Layer Statistics show circles only if there are some circles in the OASIS file.  
Sides per Donut specifies the number of edges used for donut to polygon conversion. Default is 64.  
DBU per UU is an optional integer multiple or an integer divisor of the design's database units per user units that you specify for scaling while translating an OA database to OASIS without changing the source OA database. Default is empty. Preference: dbExportOasisDbuPerUU  
<!-- image -->

metadata.Header 2: Exporting Design Data in Library Exchange Format (LEF)

content:
## Exporting Design Data in Library Exchange Format (LEF)  
Library Exchange Format (LEF) is an ASCII data format that describes standard cell libraries. LEF files typically include a technology section (rules, definitions, and capacitance), a site extension section, and a macros section (cell information, pins, blockages, and so on). LEF is used with the design exchange format (DEF), which describes netlists and circuits, to fully represent the physical layout of designs.  
To export design data in Library Exchange Format (LEF):  
1. From the Home or Console tab, choose File > Export > LEF to open the Export LEF dialog box.
2. On the Main tab, enter settings as described in Table52.
3. Click the Options tab in the Export LEF dialog box (Figure35).
