## Showing Synchronous Clone Groups  
You can show synchronous clone groups for an open design through the Design Navigator. Additionally, you can highlight group connectivity.  
To create synchronous clone groups, see instructions on working with figure groups in the Custom Compiler Layout Editor User Guide for Creating and Editing Objects .  
To show synchronous clone groups:  
1. Begin by opening the Design Navigator. (From a design layout open for editing, choose Window > Assistants > Design Navigator Assistant ).
2. In the Design Navigator with an open design containing synchronous clone groups, view the groups.  
<!-- image -->  
- a. In the Design Navigator toolbar, click the Groups button.  
By default, the system shows all groups. This icon indicates a standard figure  
- [ ] group:  
- b. From the Groups button menu (to the right of the Groups button), choose Synchronous Clones .
3. In the list of synchronous clone groups, view status.  
Synchronous clone groups appear as group icons with circling arrows:  
Clones out of synchronization with their peer group show a red x :  
<!-- image -->  
To synchronize unsynchronized clone groups, see Synchronizing Cloned Groups to Peers.  
4. Show in the design connectivity in a synchronous clone group:  
In the toolbar, click the Highlight Peer Group button, and choose a highlight color to  
apply from the drop-down menu. The color yellow has been chosen here.  
<!-- image -->  
The system applies the selected color to group names in the list of synchronous clones. The system also highlights connectivity within cloned groups on the canvas, using this color.

metadata.Header 2: Adding Figure Groups to Synchronous Groups

content:
## Adding Figure Groups to Synchronous Groups  
The two ways you can add a figure group to a synchronous group are:  
- Using the Add to Sync Group Command
- Using the Make Sync Peers Command

## Caution:  
The Add to Sync Group command and the Make Sync Peers command are available only if you choose Tools > Enable Layout Advanced .

metadata.Header 2: Using the Add to Sync Group Command

content:
## Using the Add to Sync Group Command  
In the Design Navigator, you can use the Add to Sync Group command to add selected figure groups to an existing or new synchronous group. If a figure group already belongs in a synchronous group, the command moves the figure group from the current synchronous group to the newly designated synchronous group.  
<!-- image -->  
To add figure groups to a synchronous group:  
1. In the Design Navigator, display the list of figure groups. For instructions, see Displaying the List of Figure Groups.
2. Select the figure groups.
3. Right-click the selected groups, and then choose Add to Sync Group .  
<!-- image -->  
The Add to Sync Group dialog box opens.  
<!-- image -->  
4. Do one of the following:
- In the Name list, select an existing synchronous group.
- In the Name box, type a name for the synchronous group you want to create.
5. Click Add to Sync Group . The Design Navigator Groups tab refreshes and displays the new groupings.  
<!-- image -->

metadata.Header 2: Using the Make Sync Peers Command

content:
## Using the Make Sync Peers Command  
In the Design Navigator, you can use the Make Sync Peers command to break selected figure groups from an existing synchronous group and add them to a new synchronous group. The new synchronous group is assigned a default name.  
To use the Make Sync Peers command:  
1. In the Design Navigator, display the list of figure groups. For instructions, see Displaying the List of Figure Groups.
2. Select the figure groups.
3. Right-click the selected groups, and then choose Make Sync Peers .  
<!-- image -->  
The selected figure groups are moved to the newly created synchronization group, which appears in the Groups tab with a system-assigned default name.

## Breaking Synchronization of Cloned Groups  
You can break figure group synchronization manually, or you can break the synchronization through editing of synchronized clone elements when you transfer the design to another tool, and back again.  
You can break synchronization of cloned groups when you want to work with their figure groups individually.  
<!-- image -->  
To break synchronization in synchronous cloned groups:  
1. In the Design Navigator, display the list of figure groups. For instructions, see Displaying the List of Figure Groups.
2. Display the list of synchronous clone groups. To do this:
- a. In the Design Navigator toolbar, click Groups .
- b. In the menu that appears, choose Synchronous Clones .
3. Select the name of the cloned group whose synchronization you want to break, rightclick, and choose Break Sync Clone .  
You can now edit this group without automatically applying the edits to all clones of this group.  
To synchronize the groups again, see Synchronizing Cloned Groups to Peers.

## Synchronizing Cloned Groups to Peers  
You can synchronize cloned groups to their peers again after breaking the synchronization. This option is only available for figure groups that have been created by cloning.  
To synchronize cloned groups to peers:  
1. In the Design Navigator, display the list of figure groups. For instructions, see Displaying the List of Figure Groups.
2. Locate the cloned group that is no longer synchronized ( ).
3. Select the cloned group name, right-click, and choose Sync to Peers .  
<!-- image -->  
The system synchronizes this group to its cloned peers.  
You can now edit this group, and automatically apply the edits to all clones of this group.

## Device Palette Assistant  
You can use the Device Palette assistant to drag-and-drop commonly placed devices onto the design canvas. You can create, and categorize, sets of devices on the Device Palette. (Devices that do not require added parameters can be used). You can place these device instances directly from the palette to the design canvas.  
<!-- image -->  
These sections cover:  
- Displaying the Device Palette Assistant
- Adding Favorite Devices to the Device Palette
- Placing Devices from the Palette
- Adjusting Device Palette Contents

## Displaying the Device Palette Assistant  
To display the Device Palette assistant:  
- In a layout or schematic view, choose Window > Assistants > Device Palette .  
The assistant docks along the window edge. Undock it by clicking, and dragging it.

metadata.Header 2: Adding Favorite Devices to the Device Palette

content:
## Adding Favorite Devices to the Device Palette  
You can add favorite devices to the palette to create a collection of devices and make them available directly from the palette.  
Use the Device Palette assistant to add favorite devices to the palette.  
To add a favorite device to the palette:  
1. Begin by opening the Device Palette assistant. In a layout or schematic view, choose Window > Assistants > Device Palette .
2. On the device palette, click the + button on the toolbar. The Add Device dialog box appears.
3. Specify or browse to find the library, cell, and view.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
The palette allows referencing of a master of any view type from either the layout or schematic editor. However, device favorites you add here appear in the device palette for this editor only.  
4. (Optional) Accept the suggested alias, or enter a new alias.  
Aliases provide an additional level of classification, after categories, for the devices in the palette.  
5. From the list, choose a category or enter a new category for the palette to offer.  
A new category you create here will include this favorite device.  
6. (Optional) Parameters of the device is collapsed at startup. You can click the button to expand the Parameters table.
7. Click OK to close the Add Device dialog box.

metadata.Header 2: Editing Favorite Devices in the Device Palette

content:
## Editing Favorite Devices in the Device Palette  
You can edit favorite devices in the palette.  
To edit a favorite device to the palette:  
1. Begin by opening the Device Palette assistant. In a layout or schematic view, choose Window > Assistants > Device Palette .
2. On the device palette, click the button on the toolbar. The Edit Device dialog box appears.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
3. Specify or browse to change the library, cell, and view as needed.
4. (Optional) Parameters of the device is collapsed at startup. You can click the button to expand the Parameters table.
5. Click OK to close the Edit Device dialog box.  
<!-- image -->

## Placing Devices from the Palette  
You can place a device from the device palette to quickly repeat the instance creation process for favorite devices. Use the Device Palette assistant to place commonly used devices in a design.  
To place a device from the palette:  
1. Begin by opening the Device Palette assistant. In a layout or schematic view, choose Window > Assistants > Device Palette .
2. From the Device Palette toolbar, choose the category.
3. From the palette list, use one of the three methods.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
- Select the device by name, and drag it onto the design canvas.
- Double-click the device name, fine tune instance creation options, and place the instance.
- Select the device by name, click Create Instance , fine tune instance creation options, and place the instance.  
When the palette places a device instance, it also adds it to the Recently Placed category for additional quick access.

## Adjusting Device Palette Contents  
You can adjust device palette contents by adding or deleting categories, deleting device favorites, and copying device favorites to new categories.  
To adjust device palette contents:  
1. Begin by opening the Device Palette assistant. In a layout or schematic view, choose Window > Assistants > Device Palette .
2. To the right of the Category list box, click the Browse button (...).
- Add a category by choosing <Click to Add> and entering the category name.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
- Delete a category or device favorite (by its alias) by selecting it and clicking the red x .  
The Recently Placed and Uncategorized categories cannot be deleted. However, you can delete device favorites from any category where they are listed.  
- Copy a favorite (by its alias) to another category by selecting it by name, and dragging it to the destination category.
3. Click OK .

## Error Viewer Assistant  
You can use the Error Viewer assistant to show and browse the resulting violations from physical verification tools such as DRD on the canvas.  
The Error Viewer assistant lists all violations in the marker tree and marker table pane, and shows the detailed information for each marker in the marker detail pane.  
These sections cover:  
- Opening the Error Viewer Assistant
- Using the Error Viewer Assistant in the Schematic Editor
- Managing the Marker Tree
- Viewing Marker Categories
- Viewing Error Markers
- Viewing Error Markers Hierarchically
- Manipulating Error Markers
- Sorting Error Markers
- Deleting Error Markers
- Customizing Marker Information to Display
- Showing Tooltips of Markers
- Customizing the Error Viewer Layout Style
- Viewing Markers in Shadow
- Managing Highlight Colors
- Highlighting Markers When Selecting  
- Highlighting With an X Symbol
- Setting Zoom Mode after Highlighting
- Setting Highlight Actions
- Specifying the Maximum Number of Markers to Display
- Clearing All Highlights When Closing Error Viewer
- Selecting First Item of Marker Table
- Setting Filter Type for Categories
- Loading Calibre Result
- Loading RedHawk Result
- Loading Generic Format File
- Exporting to a Text File
- Exporting Waived List

## Opening the Error Viewer Assistant  
Open the Error Viewer assistant to work with design violations (represented by oaMarker objects).  
To open the Error Viewer assistant, use one of these methods:  
- In a design, choose Window>Assistants>Error Viewer .
- Use the shortcut key Shift+E that is bound in the Laker binding set. For information about binding set selections, see Customizing Keyboard Shortcuts.  
The Error Viewer assistant pane appears on the right side of the window.  
<!-- image -->  
Figure 40 Error Viewer Assistant  
<!-- image -->  
You can undock the Error Viewer assistant pane using one of these methods:  
- Click and drag it to a required location.
- Click Dock (next to Close ).  
When redocking the floating pane to the window, you can use one of the following methods:  
- Click and drag it to the design window, or use the docking button.
- Click Pin Dock Widget (off by default) on the toolbar to only allow docking from the docking button.

metadata.Header 2: Using the Error Viewer Assistant in the Schematic Editor

content:
## Using the Error Viewer Assistant in the Schematic Editor  
Starting from W-2024.09 release, the Error Viewer assistant is the default error viewer in the Schematic Editor. Which means, the default of the seUseErrorViewer preference is true .  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
To run ERC or SRC checks on a read-only schematic design using the Error Viewer assistant to view the error markers, perform the following steps.  
1. Disable the Create Violation Markers in Designs option in the Schematic Editor Check Options dialog box.
2. Choose Window>Assistants>Error Viewer to open the assistant and use the features described in the following sections.  
To use Marker Browser Assistant as the error viewer in the Schematic Editor, set the seUseErrorViewer preference as false by typing db::setPrefValue seUseErrorViewer -value false in the Console.

## Managing the Marker Tree  
The marker tree shows marker categories along with the number of markers and the color used for categories and markers.  
The marker tree consists of the following columns: Category, Count, and Color.  
- In the Category column, markers can be classified by the following categories:  
| Category     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Design       | Shows the name of the opened design. When the Hierarchy option is enabled, the design name in bold represents the current opened design while the design name in plain represents the design at other hierarchy levels. See Viewing Error Markers Hierarchically for more details.                          |
| Tool         | Shows the tool that verifies the violations. This information is derived from the oaMarker attributes.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Severity     | Shows the severity type of violations. This information is derived from the oaMarker attributes. Severity types are fixed values as defined by OpenAccess: ◦ Error ◦ Warning ◦ Signed Off Error ◦ Information ◦ Annotation ◦ Fatal Error ◦ Critical Error ◦ Acknowledge Warning ◦ Signed Off Critical Error |
| ShortMessage | Shows the short message of markers. The short message is set as the rule ID, for example: m1.s.1. If the rule is converted from a constraint, the constraint ID is used.                                                                                                                                    |  
<!-- image -->  
| Category   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Message    | Shows the long message of markers. The long message is set as the description of the rule set. For example, the minimum spacing rule description can be Minimum metal space in MINP direction (horizontal) . If such information is not found, the tool composes a name from the original content of the rule or constraint. If the violation marker relates to spacing or width, the Error Viewer shows an actual distance and a needed distance at the beginning of the message field, as shown in the following figure, to ease the effort required for violation fixing. |  
- The Count column shows the number of markers in the corresponding category. The Error Viewer assistant shows the Count column by default. The Error Viewer displays the column title as Count(%d) where %d indicates the number of markers in the corresponding category. This column is not resizable.  
For more information on how to show the column, see Manipulating Error Markers.  
- The Color column shows the mapping highlight color for each category. The Error Viewer assistant hides the Color column by default. This column is not resizable.  
This column is available only when the By Category option is enabled for highlight colors in the Error Viewer Options dialog box.  
For information on how to assign colors to highlighted categories or markers, see Managing Highlight Colors.  
For more information on how to show the column, see Manipulating Error Markers.  
These sections cover:  
- Displaying Category Levels in the Marker Tree
- Configuring the Marker Tree Contents
- Wildcard Matching in the Display Filter

metadata.Header 2: Displaying Category Levels in the Marker Tree

content:
## Displaying Category Levels in the Marker Tree  
By default, markers are classified in the Category column by the following sequence of display levels: Design, Tool, ShortMessage, and Message.  
To change the display level of categories:  
1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window>Assistants>Error Viewer .
2. From the Category column, right-click the column header to show the category menu.
3. Click the drop-down list to the right of the categories to change the selected display levels.  
<!-- image -->  
Click OK to commit the change. The Category column is refreshed and the marker tree is collapsed.  
The category level you defined in the marker tree affects the Filter Display dialog box contents. See Configuring the Marker Tree Contents for more information.  
4. (Optional) Choose the arrow buttons next to the marker category to expand the current node's subtree and see the underlying markers in the category.  
Double-click the marker category to expand or collapse specific levels.  
For more information on showing or hiding category levels in the marker tree, see Manipulating Error Markers.

metadata.Header 2: Automatically Expanding Marker Levels in Error Viewer

content:
## Automatically Expanding Marker Levels in Error Viewer  
The Error Viewer in Custom Compiler provides a centralized interface for reviewing and managing error markers generated by various tools, such as Via Checker. Automatically expanding marker levels after loading error data streamlines the review process, allowing you to quickly access relevant error categories without manual navigation.  
You can control the default expansion level of the marker tree in the Error Viewer using the deErrorViewerAutoExpandMarkerLevel preference. This setting determines how many levels of the marker tree are expanded automatically when error markers are loaded. The default is 2.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->

## Configuring the Marker Tree Contents  
You can focus on the data that you want to focus on by using a display filter.  
To configure the marker tree contents with single or multiple categories:  
1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window>Assistants>Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Options . In the Error Viewer Options dialog box, set Filter Type as Multiple Category , and then click OK . See Setting Filter Type for Categories for more information. D
3. Click the toolbar menu and choose Filter Display .  
<!-- image -->  
The Filter Display dialog box appears.  
<!-- image -->  
Contents of the Filter Display dialog box vary when you change the category level in the marker tree, as shown in the following figure. See Displaying Category Levels in the Marker Tree for more information.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
By default, the tool uses a wildcard character * to show all of the violations in the marker tree.  
4. (Optional) Click None to deselect all severity types. Choose any of the severity types you want to display.
5. Click OK to commit the change. The marker tree is refreshed and collapsed.
6. Click the toolbar menu and choose Options . In the Error Viewer Options dialog box, set Filter Type as Single Category , and then click OK . See Setting Filter Type for Categories for more information. D  
<!-- image -->  
Now you can only filter violations from one of the available categories: Design, Tool, ShortMessage (default), and Message.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
You may enter the required filter string in the filter text box, which corresponds to Filters and Case Sensitivity settings in the General Options dialog box. See Setting General Options for more information.  
<!-- image -->

metadata.Header 2: Wildcard Matching in the Display Filter

content:
## Wildcard Matching in the Display Filter  
You can use the wildcard character * when typing a filter string in the text box, for example: G*. Click Apply to refresh the contents of the marker tree.  
| Characters   | Functions                                                                                                                                    | Examples                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| *            | Matches any sequence of zero or more characters.                                                                                             | t*t matches test or tonight but not tactic .                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ?            | Matches any single character. This is the same as "." in full regular expression (regrexps).                                                 | m?n matches man , men or min but not moon .                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [CHARS]      | Matches any character in square brackets. If CHARS contains a sequence of the form a-b, any character between a and b, inclusive, may match. | *a[ch] matches all strings that end with either ac or ah .                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| \            | Use the backslash character to escape a single character.                                                                                    | If string var equals to var="abcd\ef*g?h" • *\?* matches string that contains ? , so it matches var . • *[\]* matches string that contains \ , so it matches var . • *[12]* matches string that contain 1 or 2 , so it does not match var . |  
The tool saves the filter history (Figure41) so that you can easily choose from previously used filters.  
<!-- image -->

## Viewing Marker Categories  
You can view and highlight the categories of markers in the marker tree and the design.  
To view and highlight the categories of markers:  
1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window>Assistants>Error Viewer .
2. From the marker tree, choose the design and click Highlight Previous Category and Highlight Next Category on the toolbar to navigate to the previous or next marker category shown in the marker tree and also highlight the associated objects on the canvas.
3. (Optional) Click Clear Highlight to clear highlights of markers and their associated objects at the current design level.

## Viewing Error Markers  
You can view and highlight error markers in the marker tree and the design, and also show more detailed messages associated with the highlighted markers.  
To view and highlight error markers:  
1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window>Assistants>Error Viewer .
2. From the marker tree, choose the design or any severity type of a category (for example: CriticalError).  
(Optional) From the marker table pane, choose a marker of the selected design or category.  
3. Click Highlight Previous Marker and Highlight Next Marker on the toolbar to navigate to the previous or next marker relative to the selected category and highlight the marker and its associated object on the canvas.
4. (Optional) Click Highlight Selected Marker to highlight the selected marker and its associated object on the canvas. You can find the longer message of the highlighted marker in the lower region of the Error Viewer.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
5. (Optional) To show more than one marker or a marker category, use Ctrl+click to select each marker individually.
6. (Optional) Click Clear All Highlight to clear highlights of markers and their associated objects at the current design level.

## Viewing Error Markers Hierarchically  
By default (hierarchy disabled), the marker tree displays only the markers in the current edit design. When the Hierarchy option is on, you can view all markers from the top design hierarchy to the hierarchy that are visible down to the view depth.  
To view error markers from the top design hierarchy to down:  
1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window>Assistants>Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and choose Hierarchy . For more information about toolbar menu options, see Manipulating Error Markers. D
3. Set the stop level on the Hierarchy toolbar to 1.  
<!-- image -->  
You can specify the start and stop levels from the Design Options dialog box (see Setting Layout Design Options) or from the Start Level and Stop Level boxes on the Hierarchy toolbar.  
The Error Viewer updates the marker tree and shows the design name of the current opened design in bold text to distinguish it from designs (shown in plain text) at other hierarchy levels.  
<!-- image -->  
You can use the options available when you right-click selections from the list.  
Table70 describes the Error Viewer options menu in the marker tree for descending design levels.  
<!-- image -->  
Table 70 Error Viewer Options Menu in Marker Tree for Descending Design Levels  
| Error Viewer Menu   | Description                                                                                           |
|---------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Descend             | Moves down to a lower hierarchy level to let you view and highlight the markers at the visible depth. |
| Unsort Tree         | Restores the marker tree order to its initial state.                                                  |
| Collapse            | Collapses the selected categories.                                                                    |
| Expand              | Expands the selected categories.                                                                      |
| Hide Count Column   | Hides the Count column from the marker tree.                                                          |
| Hide Color Column   | Hides the Color column from the marker tree.                                                          |  
4. Right-click the design shown in plain text and choose Descend .  
The Error Viewer updates the marker tree and shows the design name in bold.  
Pushing and popping through the hierarchies causes the display of the marker tree to update, always showing the markers down to the visible depth.  
5. Act on the markers selected in the marker tree or the marker table pane. For more information, see Manipulating Error Markers.
6. Click the Return button on the Hierarchy toolbar to return to the upper level of the design hierarchy.  
(Optional) Click the Return to Top button on the Hierarchy toolbar to return to the top level.  
<!-- image -->

## Manipulating Error Markers  
You can manipulate error markers you have selected in the Error Viewer. The Error Viewer offers actions from the Error Viewer toolbar buttons and toolbar menu, and also through the options menu (the right-click selections).  
To manipulate error markers in the marker tree:  
1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window>Assistants>Error Viewer .
2. Act on the error markers selected in the marker tree.  
You can use the toolbar buttons and toolbar menu. You can additionally use the options available when you right-click selections from the list.

| Delete Marker                | Removes the selected marker from the marker tree and the design. The marker tree is refreshed after deletion. See Deleting Error Markers. This button is disabled if the current design is read-only.  |

## Sorting Error Markers  
You can sort error markers in descending (the default) or ascending order to easily access the ones you want to browse.  
<!-- image -->  
To sort error markers in the marker tree:  
1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window>Assistants>Error Viewer .
2. From the Category column, click the column header to sort markers in the marker tree.  
(Optional) Click the Tree View button menu and choose Unsort to restore the marker tree order to its initial state.

## Deleting Error Markers  
You can delete more than one error marker in the marker tree and remove the highlight of the marker from the canvas.  
To delete error markers:  
1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window>Assistants>Error Viewer .
2. In the Error Viewer, choose the marker you want to delete.  
(Optional) To select more than one marker or a marker category, use Ctrl+ click to select each marker individually.  
(Optional) To select a range of markers or marker categories, use Shift-click or drag-left to quickly select them.  
3. Click Delete Marker to remove the selected marker(s) from the hierarchical tree and the design.  
The tool clears the highlight of markers on the canvas and also refreshes the marker tree.

## Customizing Marker Information to Display  
You can now customize viewing the detailed information of the error markers that you have selected in the marker pane.  
To customize the detailed information of a marker:  
1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window>Assistants>Error Viewer .
2. In the Error Viewer, right-click the marker for which you want to customize the detailed information.
3. Check the information items to display from the menu, as shown in the following figure.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
The selected marker displays detailed information for only the information items that you have selected.

## Showing Tooltips of Markers  
You can show a tooltip containing the tool information, the severity type, and the short and long messages when hovering the pointer over a marker on the canvas.  
To show the tooltip of a marker:  
1. Begin by opening the Error Viewer assistant. In a design, choose Window>Assistants>Error Viewer .
2. Click the toolbar menu and make sure that Show Tip is on.
3. On the canvas, hover the pointer over the marker you want to check.  
When there are overlapped error markers, the tooltip uses the format (num1/num2) where num1 indicates the index and num2 indicates the total number of markers.  
<!-- image -->  
Use shortcut keys 1 and 2 to cyclically show the tooltip of each marker.  
<!-- image -->

You can zoom to the newly highlighted objects after enabling the Zoom Mode after Highlighting option.

The explanation strings in the result file are mapped as the marker's Message attribute if no rule file is specified or no corresponding rule information in the rule file. ## Hierarchy Navigator Assistant  
You can use the Hierarchy Navigator assistant to navigate and work in the hierarchy, by instance or master name.  
- Displaying the Hierarchy Navigator Assistant
- Setting Navigation by Instance
- Setting Navigation by Master
- Exporting Design Hierarchy
- Resolving Context Issues
- Searching Instances
- Showing Quick Access Menu

## Displaying the Hierarchy Navigator Assistant  
To display the Hierarchy Navigator in a design layout or schematic view, choose Window>Assistants>Hierarchy Navigator .  
The Hierarchy Navigator shows the hierarchy tree structure. The root of the hierarchical tree is the top library, cell, view (LCV). Each parent node contains the names of the child instances. Instances in the design are highlighted when they are selected in the Hierarchy Navigator.  
Use the heNavigatorSortOrder Tcl preference to sort instances in alphabetical order or to place the cells with no hierarchy at the bottom of the hierarchy.

## Setting Navigation by Instance  
You can set navigation by instance to work with instances only.  
<!-- image -->  
To set navigation by instance:  
1. Open the Hierarchy Navigator assistant. In a design layout or schematic view, choose Window>Assistants>Hierarchy Navigator .
2. In the toolbar, click Hierarchy by Instance to see the hierarchy of each occurrence of an instance in the design. The Hierarchy Navigator also specifies the individual bit index into a vector instance to descend into when navigating by instance. The selected index is displayed in a second column as shown in the following figure:  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
The following information is displayed in the second column based on the instances:  
- The Design Editor descends into the selected index. The column shows the index, represented in angle brackets, of any vector instance in the descend path.
- Vector instances that are not in the descend path: Shows the current default or ellipses (…) if there is no current default index.
- Other instances: Shows no information in the index. The text in the left column spans both columns.  
Click the index to show an in-line combination box with all indexes of the available vector instance. It is possible to select an index with the mouse or keyboard. You can type the number of the index for the cursor to automatically scroll and select the index from the list.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
To change the descend path in the Design Editor without prompting or redecorating the window, change the selected index in the descend path. The design is redrawn if the evaluation of any text objects depends on the descend path.  
You can show and change the index of a vector instance that is not in the descend path after the column is displayed. The default index for the next descend operation changes (without descending into the instance) when the index of a vector instance that is not in the descend path changes. This index serves as the default for all descend operations, including the ide::descend preference, the de::descend preference, and by double-clicking within the Hierarchy Navigator .  
3. Double-click the instance to descend into the selected instance. Right-click on an instance to show the following menu:  
<!-- image -->  
From this menu, select the following option to perform edits:  
- Edit or view the designs in the hierarchy by choosing Descend Edit or Descend Read
- Edit the instance in place by choosing Edit in Place (available when the edit and the selected view designs match).
- Zoom to the selected master by choosing Fit . If the selected master does not exist within the edit design, Fit zooms to its parent master within the edit design.
- Set a design as the view design by choosing Set View Design (available when the edit and the selected view designs match).
- Select or deselect the instance in the canvas by choosing Select in Design or Deselect in Design .

## Setting Navigation by Master  
You can set navigation by master to work with master instances only.  
To navigate by master:  
1. Open the Hierarchy Navigator assistant. In a design layout or schematic view, choose Window > Assistants > Hierarchy Navigator .
2. In the toolbar, click the Hierarchy by Master  
<!-- image -->  
.  
To display the list of masters used in the design, and their hierarchy. The Hierarchy by Master mode shows the structure of the design.  
When many instances of a single master are used in a design, only one row is shown in the tree, and the instance count is shown between brackets if the master is not root.  
In the design hierarchy list, right-click on a master to show the following menu:  
<!-- image -->  
From this menu, select the following option to perform edits:  
- Open the master in the Hierarchy Editor or Design Editor option by choosing Open or Open Read Only .
- Zoom to the selected master by choosing Fit . If the selected master does not exist within the edit design, Fit zooms to its parent master within the edit design.
- Select or deselect the master in the canvas by choosing Select in Design or Deselect in Design . If the selected master does not exist within the edit design, it selects or deselects the parent master within the edit design.  
The PCell submasters are not displayed as separate masters in the Hierarchy by Master display mode.  
While in the Hierarchy by Master mode, you can open the design in a new editor window by double-clicking a master. However, it is not possible to change the design editor's context from the Hierarchy by Master display mode.

## Exporting Design Hierarchy  
You can export the design hierarchy structure to a text file.  
<!-- image -->  
To export the design hierarchy:  
1. Begin by opening the Hierarchy Navigator assistant. In a design layout or schematic view, choose Window>Assistants>Hierarchy Navigator .
2. In the toolbar, click Export Hierarchy .  
<!-- image -->  
This opens the Export Hierarchy dialog box.  
<!-- image -->  
To select the type of hierarchy structure to export use the drop-down list with Type .  
In the text file with the exported hierarchy, the default delimiter between the instance names and their paths is a single space. To use any other delimiter, such as an underscore (\_), specify it in the Delimiter tab. To view the file with the exported hierarchy structure in the Text Viewer tool, select Open in Text Editor . Click OK to open the file.

## Resolving Context Issues  
There are three types of context issues that can occur while working with designs.  
You can use the Hierarchy Navigator to resolve the following issues.  
- Invalid Contexts: If the context of the current edit or view design becomes invalid (due to change in the parent lineage), the Hierarchy Navigator prunes all the submodules of invalid instances from the tree except instances in the lineage of the current edit context.
- Out of context lineages: Instances can be pushed out-of-context while working with the design. The Hierarchy Navigator indicates the out-of-context instances by a red color font.
- Invalid Placed/Switched Masters: If the placed or switched master does not exist, the instance/master is displayed in a red color font. If the master name is visible, the placed master is displayed instead of the switched master.  
<!-- image -->

## Searching Instances  
To find instances in the design hierarchy:  
1. Begin by opening the Hierarchy Navigator assistant. In a design layout or schematic view, choose Window>Assistants>Hierarchy Navigator .
2. In the toolbar, click Show Search Line , which shows or hides the Find text field.  
<!-- image -->  
Type an initial of the instance name you want to locate, for example:  
<!-- image -->  
Filtering adheres to the Find preference setting of the General Options dialog box for partial match, wildcard, regular expression, and match start. See Setting General Options.  
<!-- image -->

## Showing Quick Access Menu  
The Hierarchy Navigator allows you to access frequently used commands when you rightclick an instance.  
To show the menu:  
1. Open the Hierarchy Navigator assistant. In a design layout or schematic view, choose Window>Assistants>Hierarchy Navigator .
2. In the design hierarchy list, right-click on an instance to show the following menu:  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
- Open the selected instance in another window by choosing Open or Open Read Only .
- Edit the selected instance directly in the same window by choosing Edit in Place .
- Zoom to the selected instance by choosing Fit . If the selected instance does not exist within the edit design, Fit zooms to its parent instance within the edit design.
- Select or deselect the instance in the canvas by choosing Select in Design or Deselect in Design .

## Object Filter Assistant  
You can use the Object Filter assistant to control the way the system responds to the selection of specific object types. The Object Filter works with schematic and symbol views.  
If you are working in an area of a schematic where you cannot select a wire due to the interference of bounding boxes, you can use the Object Filter to turn off bounding box object selection, and more easily allow wire selection.  
You can also use the Object Filter during area selection, for example, in situations where you might want to select a group of instances, and exclude wires, and other objects, from the selection set.  
This topic describes the following:  
- Opening the Object Filter Assistant
- Filtering Schematic Objects
- Filtering Symbol Objects

## Opening the Object Filter Assistant  
Open the Object Filter to work with object selection settings in schematics and symbols.  
To open the Object Filter:  
- In the schematic or symbol, choose Window>Assistants>Schematic Object Filter or Symbol Object Filter .  
The assistant docks along the window edge. Undock it by clicking and dragging it.

To filter schematic objects:

2. Choose an option:  
To enable or disable individual selectability for an object, click its check box.  
To enable or disable selectability for all objects, click the buttons ( ) at the top. 回 回

2. Choose an option:

## Object/Layer Panel Assistant  
You can use the Object/Layer Panel (OLP) in layouts to:  
- Locate layer purpose pairs (LPPs), layers, and objects
- Display multiple built-in and user-defined LPP sets
- Create, edit, or remove user-defined LPP sets
- Make LPP sets, active LPP, and object types visible and selectable
- Filter LPPs, layers, objects, and mask color
- Sort the list of active LPPs
- Display more LPPs and LPP sets at a time when using Compact View  
<!-- image -->  
- Toggle between using design settings and technology settings
- Control via and instance selections
- Control the visibility and selectability of objects
- Redraw the canvas after changes are made within the OLP
- View the display packets associated with LPPs
- Reload the display resource file  
Each design has an Object/Layer Panel. Settings you make apply immediately, and are stored in the technology database.  
This topic describes the following:  
- Opening the Object/Layer Panel Assistant
- Manipulating the Object/Layer Panel
- Locating LPPs, Layers, and Objects
- Displaying Color Annotations
- Displaying Presets
- Working With LPPs
- System LPPs
- Working With Layers
- Working With Objects
- Sharing OLP Settings
- Controlling Area Selections of Figure Groups
- Working With Display Resources
- Setting OLP Options  
<!-- image -->  
The Object/Layer Panel opens automatically with design layout views.  
This video tutorial shows how to display,select and manage LPPs using the various options available for layers and objects.  
<!-- image -->

## Opening the Object/Layer Panel Assistant  
The Object/Layer Panel opens automatically with design layout views. You can also open it manually as follows:  
In a design layout view, choose Window>Assistants>Object/Layer Panel .  
The Object/Layer Panel docks on the right side of the design window. Undock it by clicking and dragging it to a required location.  
Figure 42 Object/Layer Panel Assistant  
<!-- image -->

## Manipulating the Object/Layer Panel  
The Object/Layer Panel offers actions from the Object/Layer Panel toolbar and also through the toolbar menu.  
To manipulate the Object/Layer Panel:  
1. Begin by opening the Object/Layer Panel assistant. In a design layout view, choose Window>Assistants>Object/Layer Panel .
2. Act on the objects or LPPs in the Object/Layer Panel.  
<!-- image -->  
You can use the toolbar boxes and toolbar menu.  
Table83 describes actions you can perform using Object/Layer Panel toolbar boxes.  
Table 83 Object/Layer Panel Toolbar Boxes and their Actions  
| Selection   | Action                                                                      |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|             | Set the visibility for all objects or LPPs or only those that are valid.    |
|             | Set the selectability for all objects or LPPs or only those that are valid. |  
You can use the leOLPShowActionsToolbar Tcl preference to display or hide the Visible and Select options.  
<!-- image -->  
Table84 describes actions you can perform using the Object/Layer Panel toolbar menu .  
Table 84 Object/Layer Panel Toolbar Menu Options  
| Menu Option                  | Description                                                                                                                          |
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| OLP Options                  | Opens the Object Layer Panel dialog box. See Setting OLP Options.                                                                    |
| Make Visible LPPs Selectable | Makes all currently visible LPPs selectable.                                                                                         |
| Display Resource Editor      | Opens the Display Resource Editor tool for the current design. See Working With Display Resources for help using this option.        |
| Reload Display               | Reloads the modified display resource file to the Object/Layer Panel. See Working With Display Resources for help using this option. |

## Locating LPPs, Layers, and Objects  
Using the Object/Layer Panel, you can use the filter box to locate LPPs, layers, and objects in the LPPs , Layers , and Objects tabs separately. The filter applies to the current tab. When switching tabs, the filter applies to the new tab.  
<!-- image -->  
To locate LPPs, layers, and objects:  
1. Begin by opening the Object/Layer Panel assistant. In a design layout view, choose Window>Assistants>Object/Layer Panel .
2. In the Object/Layer Panel, click one of the following tabs:
- LPPs tab that displays the list of LPPs in the design
- Layers tab that displays the list of layers in the design
- Objects tab that displays the list of objects in the design  
When switching the LPPs , Layers , and Objects tabs, the filter applies to the tab you are currently in.  
3. (Optional) To view more LPPs at once, you can resize the Object/Layer Panel by adjusting its width so that the LPPs are listed in several visible columns.
4. (Optional) From the toolbar menu , make sure that the Show LPP Filter option is on.  
<!-- image -->  
The Object/Layer Panel shows the filter box by default. You can deselect Show LPP Filter to hide the filter.  
5. In the filter box, type the full or partial text or an expression to search for the items of interest. See Using Filter Boxes for help using this filter.  
When locating LPPs or layers, use a space to apply filtering to the layer name and purpose name, for example: m* dr* matches LPP metal1 drawing (which is the closest match), and other LPPs starting with layer name m and purpose dr .  
When finding route related objects in a list of object types, first click the Objects tab, and then type route in the filter box.  
6. With the list of components you want to use now optionally filtered, select them in the Object/Layer Panel.
7. Use the Object/Layer Panel to act on the selected components.  
When you are ready to act on the selected components, see the following sections:  
- Working With LPPs
- Working With Layers
- Working With Objects  
<!-- image -->

## Displaying Color Annotations  
You can display or hide color annotations in your design. By default, color annotations appear as colored outlines surrounding shapes to indicate the colors that are assigned to the shapes. However, you can change how the annotations appear using the Packets settings in the Display Resource Editor. For more information, see Display Resource Editor Tool.  
In Figure43, color annotations are displayed for shapes a and b using the default annotation settings. Shape a has a red outline, indicating that it is assigned color1. Shape b has a blue outline, indicating that it is assigned color2. The remaining shapes in this example are not annotated.  
Figure 43 Color Annotations Displayed for Shapes a and b  
<!-- image -->  
To display color annotations:  
1. Begin by opening the Object/Layer Panel assistant. In a design layout view, choose Window>Assistants>Object/Layer Panel .
2. Click the toolbar menu choose Show Mask Color Filter to show the Color toolbar at the top of the Object/Layer Panel. D  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
3. Click one of the following to display color annotations:  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
| Button   | Description                                                                |
|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|          | Displays annotations of shapes that are assigned the Red color.            |
|          | Displays annotations of shapes that are assigned the Blue color.           |
|          | Displays annotations of shapes that are assigned the Green color.          |
|          | Displays annotations of shapes that are assigned the Same color.           |
|          | Displays only the color annotations of shapes whose colors are locked.     |
|          | Displays only the color annotations of shapes whose colors are not locked. |  
For information on how to assign colors to shapes, see the Custom Compiler Layout Editor User Guide for Creating and Editing Objects for details.

## Displaying Presets  
You can display or hide the Presets toolbar.  
A preset is a named collection of state information in the Object/Layer Panel which can be restored en masse. A preset contains:  
- Selected LPP sets and their relationship
- LPP visibility, selectability, and fill status
- Object filter visibility and selectability status  
A preset can be created from the current design state using the de::createOLPPreset Tcl command. It is not possible to create one programmatically outside of manipulating the design and then capturing its state.  
To display a preset status information:  
1. Begin by opening the Object/Layer Panel assistant. In a design layout view, choose Window>Assistants>Object/Layer Panel .
2. Click the toolbar menu choose Show Presets to show the Presets toolbar at the top of the Object/Layer Panel. D  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
On the Presets toolbar, D stands for Default, and it is the default setting of LPP list (or selected LPPs) in the design that is opened. The preset number are user-saved LPP selection settings that apply globally. Click the button to add more preset number. +  
<!-- image -->  
3. You can set your own LPP selection settings and then right-click one of the numbered preset buttons to save the settings.  
Right-clicking preset button shows a Save button to save the user-defined LPP selection settings.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
You can remove or rename an existing user-saved LPP selection settings preset by right-clicking the numbered button for the user-saved preset.  
<!-- image -->  
You can activate multiple presets at a time by saving multiple numbered buttons. You can merge an active preset with the current LPP settings by clicking the corresponding numbered button while pressing the Shift key. To delete or subtract this preset setting from the current LPP settings, click the corresponding numbered button while pressing the Ctrl key. You must click the least-numbered button to merge or delete.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
Presets in the Object tab are saved and loaded through the application state interface defined by deOLPPresets.xml . You will be prompted to save the preset settings with the Object/Layer Panel Presets option when closing the software.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->

## Working With LPPs  
In the LPPs tab, you can:  
- Display multiple built-in and user-defined layer LPP sets  
LPP sets are sorted alphanumerically. LPP sets with no default LPP are shown first, followed by a small separator, and then the LPP sets which have default LPPs. The LPP sets with default LPPs are sorted in mask order of the default LPPs.  
- Create, edit, or remove user-defined LPPs
- Make active LPPs visible and selectable
- Show abbreviations and stream layer numbers of LPPs
- Change the drawing priority of an LPP
- Show or hide LPPs with specified purposes
- Sort the list of active LPPs
- Control the visibility and selectability of boundary objects  
The LPPs tab consists of two panes. The upper pane shows the built-in LPP sets and the user-defined LPP sets. The lower pane shows the contained LPPs of a selected LPP set.  
The following sections cover:  
- Using LPPs Tab Menu
- Creating User-Defined LPP Sets
- Editing User-defined LPP Sets
- Removing User-defined LPP Sets
- Setting the Active Layer Purpose Pair
- Making LPP Sets Visible and Selectable
- Showing Abbreviations and Stream Layer Numbers
- Changing the Drawing Priority of a Layer Purpose Pair
- Sorting Layer Purpose Pairs
- Controlling the Visibility and Selectability of Boundary Objects  
<!-- image -->

## Using LPPs Tab Menu  
To use the LPPs tab menu:  
1. Begin by opening the Object/Layer Panel assistant. In a design layout view, choose Window>Assistants>Object/Layer Panel .
2. Click the LPPs tab and then click the tab menu. Table85 describes the LPPs menu options.  
Table 85 LPPs Tab Menu Options  
| LPPs Menu Option   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

This set is always available.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

See Editing User-defined LPP Sets for help editing user-defined LPP sets.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Remove LPP Set     | Available only when one or more LPP sets are selected and none of them are system-defined. See Removing User-defined LPP Sets for help removing LPP sets.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

| Show All LPP Sets  | Displays all LPP sets, including those previously hidden, in the LPPs tab.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| AND Selected Sets  | Filters LPPs that are used in the current design by making an intersection of two or more selected LPP sets. This option works for all LPP sets including system-reserved and user-defined LPP sets. You can also type the following line in the console to show the intersection of selected sets (for example: lpp_set1 and lpp_set2) on the Object/Layer Panel: db::setPrefValue leLPPSet -value "lpp_set1 * lpp_set2" |
| Show LPP Sets      | Displays the upper pane of LPP Sets in the LPPs tab.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Show Stream Layer Numbers | When enabled, the tool shows the stream layer and data type numbers in a tooltip, rather than showing the OpenAccess layer and purpose numbers, if the layer mapping file is found. If the layer mapping file is not found, the tool checks if the purpose is system reserved and if there is a mapping for the LPP and then uses it as the stream layer or data type number.
