## Setting Up the DTCO Parameters  
You can use the Parameters tab to display, define, import and export values for DTCO parameters.  
All DTCO parameters are stored with the library in its data.dm file. If a parameter affects the layout of any cell in the library, then that becomes a CDF parameter. A DTCO parameter can be dependent on one or more DTCO parameters. This dependency is captured by a Tcl expression sting as the value and has a Type called expression . A DTCO parameter is independent if the value is not a Tcl expression string and a Type other than expression .  
This topic describes the following:  
- Displaying and Filtering the DTCO Parameters
- Adding and Editing DTCO Parameters
- Exporting and Importing DTCO Parameters
- Loading DTCO Parameters
- Saving DTCO Parameters

metadata.Header 2: Displaying and Filtering the DTCO Parameters

content:
## Displaying and Filtering the DTCO Parameters  
You can view the DTCO parameters in the Parameters tab to begin to work with them.  
To view parameters:  
1. In the Parameters tab, choose library in the Library selection field. In a DTCO flow, all the DTCO parameters are defined, created, and stored in the reference library.
2. Choose Import (Exporting and Importing DTCO Parameters) or Load (Loading DTCO Parameters) to import the stored parameters.
3. All the parameters associated with the library are displayed in the parameters table.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
The parameters table shows the following parameter information: Prompt , Name , Category , Type , Value , Collection , Measure , Unit , SWB Name , Variability Type , Var Value , and Layout Parameter Name . To edit the parameter value, see Adding and Editing DTCO Parameters.  
You can filter the parameters table by Category column. To filter the parameters table, specify the string in the Filter by Category text field. After specifying the string in the text field, the tool lists the DTCO parameters that match the filter criteria.  
<!-- image -->

## Adding and Editing DTCO Parameters  
To edit DTCO parameters in the parameters table:  
1. Double-click any column in the parameter table to display the Edit Parameter dialog box. Or click the button to enable the Edit Parameter dialog box.
2. Edit the parameters in the Edit Parameter dialog box and click OK to implement the changes.  
<!-- image -->  
To add DTCO parameters in the parameters table:  
1. Right-click the parameter table to display the menu as below.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
Or click the button to enable the Add Parameter dialog box.  
<!-- image -->  
2. Specify the parameter information in the Add Parameter dialog box.
3. Click OK to add new parameters.  
The parameters that have been changed and added appear in red with italic type.  
<!-- image -->  
4. Save the design after editing. See Saving DTCO Parameters.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
If switching the library without saving the changes, the Save Library dialog box is displayed to save or discard the changes.  
<!-- image -->

## Parameters Toolbars  
Parameters toolbars let you quick edit the parameter table. Performs add parameter, delete, move, and edit the parameters in the table.  
<!-- image -->

## Exporting and Importing DTCO Parameters  
You can export the DTCO parameters to a YAML file by choosing the Export option. The Export dialog box is displayed to specify the library.  
<!-- image -->  
The exported parameters information can be edited by text editor.

metadata.Header 2: Here is the example of YAML file:

content:
## Here is the example of YAML file:  
```
#DTCO Parameters Version:0.0 Parameters: cellArchitecture: prompt:Cell Architecture type:string collection:list value:shortmedium tall layoutParameterName:cellStyle cellHeightMultiplier: prompt:CellHeightMultiplier type:float collection:list value:5.56.57.5 cellHeight: prompt:Cel1 Height type:expression collection:list value: -"[lindex$cellHeightMultiplier0]*$mOPitch" -"[lindex$cellHeightMultiplier1]*$mOPitch" -"[lindex$cellHeightMultiplier 2]*$mOPitch" measure:length unit:nm
```  
When the YAML file is created in the associated library, you can import the parameters saved in the YAML file.  
<!-- image -->  
To import a YAML file:  
1. Choose Import to display the Import dialog box.
2. Choose the YAML file in the associated library in the Import dialog box.
3. The parameters are displayed in the parameters table.  
<!-- image -->

## Loading DTCO Parameters  
To load the stored parameters:  
1. Select a library in the Library selection field.
2. Choose Load to load the data.dm associated with the library from disk.
3. The stored parameters are displayed in the parameter table.

## Saving DTCO Parameters  
You can save the edited or imported DTCO parameters by choosing the Save option. The parameters are saved in a data.dm file associated with the library. Running any computation flows from other DTCO tabs would only consume the saved parameters or values.  
<!-- image -->

## Running Transistor Modeling  
This feature creates a spice model using the TCAD tools. To generate a compact spice mode, you need IV CV data for the transistor geometry and its corresponding material description.

## Note:  
The transistor modeling flow does not need any layout design.  
In the transistor modeling flow, you can choose to run:  
- Only the IV CV data generation.
- Or only the Compact Model generation.
- Or both IV CV data and Compact Model generations.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->

## To create transistor modeling:  
1. Specify the directory in the Run Root Dir field where files related to IV CV curve and the Compact Model generation are stored.
2. Enable IV CV to select IV CV curve generation or disable IV CV to ignore the IV CV curve generation.  
To run the IV CV curve generation, specify the following settings:  
| Option             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Run Mode           | Specifies one of the following modes: ◦ gui: Select this option to launch the Sentaurus Workbench Graphical User Interface. The Transistor Modeling need to be run manually. ◦ batch: Select this option to run in the background and status can be checked in Job Monitor. |
| Queue              | To select the Queue name where the computation would be performed.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| DTCO Parameters    | Library : Specifies the library to load the DTCO parameters for the transistor modeling. Category : When the library of DTCO parameters is specified, the parameters in the transistor category are used.                                                                   |
| Template Directory | Specifies the directory contains the files for Sentaurus TCAD tool to run the transistor modeling.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Tech Type          | Specifies the technology name or label.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Variability        | The Nominal option is specified.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Threads            | Specifies the number of threads.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Project Name       | This filed is automatically populated by Tech Type and Variability .                                                                                                                                                                                                        |  
3. Enable Compact Model to select Compact Model generation or disable Compact Model to ignore the Compact Model generation.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->

metadata.Header 2: To run the Compact Model generation, specify the following settings:

content:
## To run the Compact Model generation, specify the following settings:  
| Option             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Run Mode           | Specifies one of the following modes: ◦ gui: Select this option to launch the Sentaurus Workbench Graphical User Interface. The Transistor Modeling need to be run manually. ◦ batch: Select this option to run in the background and status can be checked in Job Monitor.                                     |
| Queue              | To select the Queue name where the computation would be performed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Path File          | This field is enabled when Compact Model is checked and IV CV is not checked. Specifies the file which contains information for IV CV run. If IV CV is checked, the path information is passed from IV CV run to Compact Model run.                                                                             |
| DTCO Parameters    | Library : Specifies the library to load the DTCO parameters for compact model generation. If IV CV is checked, the library of DTCO parameters is passed from IV CV run to Compact Model run. Category : When the library of DTCO parameters is specified, the parameters in the compactModel category are used. |
| Template Directory | Specifies the directory contains the files for Sentaurus TCAD tool to run the compact model generation.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Project Name       | The final spice file of Compact Model run is stored with the Project Name directory in the Run Root Directory.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Save in Library    | Enables the option to save a cell view of the final spice model in the DTCO Library with specified Cell Name .                                                                                                                                                                                                  |  
4. Click Run to process the transistor modeling flow.

## Running Interconnect Characterization  
The interconnect characterization flow builds an integration with the TCAD tools to create interconnect structures, simulate through the process flow, run field extraction and create an ITF file. The ITF is compiled with grdgenxo (StarRC) to prepare a NXTGRD file which can be used in the digital implementation flow.  
<!-- image -->  
To create or update a NXTGRD file for parasitic extraction in the implementation flow, specify the following options and fields:  
<!-- image -->  
| Option       | Description                                                                                       |
|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Run Root Dir | Specify the directory where files related to Interconnect Characterization generation are stored. |  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
| Option             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Run Mode           | Specify the Run Mode by selecting one of the following options: • gui : Select this option to manually run the Interconnect Characterization in the Sentaurus Workbench graphical user interface. • batch : Select this option to run the Interconnect Characterization in the background and check the result in Job Monitor. |
| DTCO Parameters    | Specify the Library to load the DTCO parameters for Interconnect characterization.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Project Name       | When specifying the Project Name , the directory with project name is created in Run Root Dir to run the Interconnect Characterization.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Template Directory | Specifies the directory contains the files for Sentaurus TCAD tool to run the Interconnect Characterization.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Flow File          | Specifies the file contains the layer information with correct layer order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Headers File       | Specifies the file contains the information (technology, foundry, process node, process version, process type, process corner, and temperature) regarding the ITF header.                                                                                                                                                      |
| Materials File     | Specifies the file contains information (dielectrics, conductors, bulk resistivity model parameters, bulk resistivity, and temperature dependence) about the physical properties specific to the material needs to be simulated in the Sentaurus Workbench.                                                                    |
| Processes          | Specifies the number of jobs to be launched to run the Interconnect Characterization.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Save in Library    | The output of Interconnect characterization (NXTGRD, ITF) files are placed in interconnect_results directory. If this option is enabled and Cell Name is provided, the tool creates cell views of NXTGRD and ITF files in the DTCO Parameters Library .                                                                        |  
To generate the output of Interconnect characterization, click Run to process the implementation flow.

## Running Cell Parasitic Extraction  
After completing the layout for a standard cell, you can create the post layout extraction netlist to be used for library characterization. The extraction includes the following information. An important intermediate step between the standard cell layout and extraction is to ensure that the GDS that is generated for extraction using Raphael-FX has all the necessary layers for the process steps.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
To create or update the post layout extraction netlist, specify the following options and fields:  
| Option       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Run Root Dir | Specifies the directory where files related to the Cell Parasitic Extraction are stored.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Steam        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Export       | When this option is enabled, specify the standard cell Library / Cell / View of layout. The tool exports GDS stream before running the cell parasitic extraction. You can click the Config button to display the Export Stream dialog box. See Export > Exporting Design Data on GDSII Stream Format in Custom Compiler Environment User Guide If Export is disabled, specify the GDS stream file (*.GDS) and cell name to run the cell parasitic extraction. |
| Netlist      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Export       | When this option is enabled, specify the standard cell Library / Cell / View of schematic. The HSPICE Netlister is used for the given View Search List and View Stop List to generate the netlist file. If Export is disabled, specify the name of the netlist file (*.spi | *.lvs) to run the cell parasitic extraction.                                                                                                                                |
| Setup        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Run Mode     | Specifies the Run Mode by selecting one of the following options: • gui : Select this option to manually run the Cell Parasitic Extraction in the Sentaurus Workbench graphical user interface. • batch : Select this option to run the Cell Parasitic Extraction in the background and check the result in Job Monitor.                                                                                                                                      |
| Queue        | Specifies the Queue name where the computation would be performed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |  
<!-- image -->  
| Option                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Setup Files Input Mode | Parasitic extraction setup is typically specified through a prefs.xml file. If Library is specified, the setup files are picked from Stream/Netlist Library libpath/prefs.xml. The preference is Stream first and next is netlist. If File is specified, the setup files are picked from runDir/prefs.xml. If both export stream and export netlist are disabled, the mode switches to File . |
| Template Directory     | Specifies the directory contains the files for Sentaurus TCAD tool to run the Cell Parasitic Extraction.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Materials File         | Specifies the file contains information (dielectrics, conductors, bulk resistivity model parameters, bulk resistivity, and temperature dependence) about the physical properties specific to the material needs to be simulated in the Sentaurus Workbench.                                                                                                                                   |
| Process File           | Specifies a binary file describing the process which is provided as TCAD tool setup.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Layout Config File     | Specifies a file contains layer name mappings provided as TCAD tool setup.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Raphael Config File    | This file contains user settings for Process Explorer (meas_RC) and Raphael used for FinFET flow.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Layout Layers File     | Specifies a file contains layer numbers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ％ Processes            | Specifies the number of jobs to run the Cell Parasitic Extraction.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Output                 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Save in Library        | If this option is enabled, the output of Cell Parasitic Extraction files are placed in RunRootDirectory/CellName for a standard cell.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |  
To generate the output of Cell Parasitic Extraction, click Run to process the extraction flow.

## Running Digital Implementation  
The Digital Implementation defines a set of sample digital designs to be run through the implementation flow. The step abstracts the notion of implementation and lets you define scripts that achieve the result. You can specify the following information in this tab:  
- Fusion Compiler Technology File
- NDM Libraries (timing, power and physical information related to standard cells)
- Parasitic Files (TLU+ or NXTGRD)  
Two methods are provided for the optimization: a simplified but less flexible step or a fully customized script by using Custom Script option.  
1. Simplified Digital Implementation Flow: In this flow, you specify the library and design name, directory path where all verilog files are available, a config file, a compile file, QoR directory, and QoR result file. The tool generates a simple script to run these into an 'fc\_shell', and then invoke the QoR script on the results generated by Fusion Compiler. It requires users to put specific setup and place and route tcl flows in the config file and compile file in exchange for simple flow.
2. Custom Script Flow: A production digital implementation flow relies on other automation elements, such as makefiles, grid management, environment variables. In this flow, you specify the library and design name, and a custom script. The script is an entry point for you to setup and manage the complexities of a production flow. The tool passes rest of the arguments filled in the Digital Implementation tab as a YAML file to this script. The script may parse and get values from this YAML file.  
The output of Fusion Compiler is analyzed to generate a YAML file which contains relevant key-value pairs for comparing in Compare Split . See Comparing Split Results.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
To run the Digital Implementation, specify the following options and fields:  
1. Specify the directory in the Run Root Dir field where files related to Digital Implementation are stored.
2. Specify a file contains technology-specific information such as names, characteristics for each metal layer, and design rules in the Tech File field. This information are required to route a design.
3. Specify NDM libraries that contain the timing, power and physical information related to standard cells in the Reference Libraries section. You can add the reference library by clicking Click to Add . You can enable the library in the Enable column to specify what libraries are reference.  
<!-- image -->  
You also can use the toolbars to adjust the Reference Libraries table. The table includes the following options:  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
Table 108 Digital Implementation Toolbars  
| Option   |                  | Description                                                                                                        |
|----------|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|          | Check Selected   | Lets you enable the selected libraries to be reference libraries.                                                  |
|          | Uncheck Selected | Lets you disable the selected libraries to be reference libraries.                                                 |
|          | Add File         | Lets you add a new row and open the Select Library dialog box to specify the reference library in the created row. |
|          | Delete Selected  | Lets you delete the selected row.                                                                                  |
|          | Move Top         | Lets you move the selected row to the start of the table.                                                          |
|          | Move Up          | Lets you move the selected row up.                                                                                 |
|          | Move Down        | Lets you move the selected row down.                                                                               |
|          | Move Bottom      | Lets you move the selected row to the end of the table.                                                            |  
4. Specify the mapping file in the Layer Map File field. The mapping file contains physical layer mapping information between the input database and the specified NXTGRD file.  
(Optional) Specify NXTGRD or TLU+ files that contain the modeled layers of a circuit. You can add the files by clicking Click to Add and enable the file in the Enable column to specify what files are used. You can use the toolbar to adjust the Parasitic Files table. See Table108.  
5. In the Designs section, enable the Custom Script option to specify the script which contains the information to run the Fusion Compiler in the Designs table. Or disable the Custom Script option to specify RTL, Config files, Compile files and output QOR(Result) directory in the Designs table.  
<!-- image -->  
When disabling the Custom Script option, the Designs table includes the following fields:  
| Option            | Description                                                                                                                                |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Enable            | Lets you enable the files to run for digital flows.                                                                                        |
| DTCO Library      | Lets you specify the library name for running digital flows.                                                                               |
| Design            | Lets you specify the design name for running digital flows.                                                                                |
| Verilog Directory | Lets you specify the Design Verilog file which is input to the Fusion Compiler.                                                            |
| Config File       | Lets you specify the file that contains information about NDM library configuration MCMM setup, optional floor plan and place route setup. |
| Compile File      | Lets you specify the file that contains commands to run Fusion Compiler and place the results in QOR (result) directory.                   |
| QOR Result        | Lets you specify the directory to store the Fusion Compiler results.                                                                       |
| QOR Summary       | Lets you specify the YAML file that contains summary of the digital run, generated by QOR Exec .                                           |  
You can add the files by clicking Click to Add . The added files can be used by selecting the checkboxes in the Enable column. You can use the toolbar to adjust the Designs table. See Table108.  
6. Specify the directory in the QOR Exec field. The Quality of Result exec file parses the QOR result directory and constructs the QOR.yaml file (see Figure55) used for Compare Split. See Comparing Split Results.
7. Click Run to process the Digital Implementation flow.

## Creating a Split  
The tool picks a set of independent DTCO parameters whose values are changed from current nominal values. Only independent DTCO parameters are candidates for participating in a Split.  
After specifying a set of updated values for DTCO parameters, you can specify a new target library from a process Create Split which is created by clicking the Run button. This creates a copy of all cells that designs in the source library with the target library name and remaster instances to come from the target library. All cells in the source library (even if they are in other libraries) are copied to the target library.  
<!-- image -->  
To create a split from DTCO parameters:  
1. Specify the source library to be copied in the Source Library selection field.
2. Specify the target library name in the Target Library Name text field. It is important to name the Target Library with indicative name which tells about DTCO parameters that have been changed in the corresponding split.
3. Click the Browse button in the Target Library Directory text field to specify the target library directory from the Select Target Library Directory dialog box.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
4. (Optional) View names specified in the Exclude Views text field are not copied during a split operation.
5. Using Click to Add to add new row in the DTCO parameter table.
6. Add DTCO parameters by clicking the arrow from each row in the DTCO parameter table.  
<!-- image -->  
The table contains the following columns and toolbar:  
<!-- image -->  
| Option   | Description                                                                                             |
|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Name     | Selects one or more independent DTCO parameters from the source library by clicking the arrow.          |
| Value    | Displays the values of parameters when the parameters are specified. New values can be added or edited. |  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
| Option           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ReRun DTCO Steps | Based on the modified parameters, this column reruns steps affected by the changes to the DTCO parameter. This information relies on the Category attribute of the DTCO parameter with the correct values. |
|                  | Deletes the selected row.                                                                                                                                                                                  |  
7. If the split involves changes to the setups to the TCAD process simulations that are not exposed as DTCO parameters, then specifies the information to be updated for Parasitic Extraction , Transistor Modeling , and Interconnect Characterization in the Setup section. The values entered for various files are stored in the corresponding source library and the corresponding xml file (libraryName/tcad\_prefs.xml).
8. (Optional) The Post Callback Procedure Name is provided to execute a callback after completing Create Split process. The callback procedure has a signature of source library name, target library name and list of DTCO parameters with name, old value, and new value for each parameter that was specified into the Create Split dialog box.
9. Click Run to split to a new library which copied all cells from the source library.  
<!-- image -->

## Comparing Split Results  
The Compare Split function compares the results of QOR summary files and baseline data. The Digital Implementation flow generates a result file (QOR summary) in a simple YAML format of key-value pairs. See Running Digital Implementation.  
Figure 55 Example of QOR Summary File  
<!-- image -->  
QOR summary files from different runs in the Digital Implementation flow are compared.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
To compare the QOR summary files:  
1. Add the QOR summary files from different runs in the Digital Implementation flow to be compared in the Result Files section by clicking Click to Add . Each summary file is listed in a row in the table.  
To edit the table, use the following options:  
<!-- image -->  
| Option   |                 | Description                                                                                                |
|----------|-----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|          | Add File        | Lets you add a new row and open the Select File dialog box to specify the summary file in the created row. |
|          | Delete Selected | Lets you delete the selected row.                                                                          |
|          | Move Top        | Lets you move the selected row to the start of the table.                                                  |
|          | Move Up         | Lets you move the selected row up.                                                                         |
|          | Move Down       | Lets you move the selected row down.                                                                       |
|          | Move Bottom     | Lets you move the selected row to the end of the table.                                                    |  
2. To compare all the QOR summary files, click the Report button. The compared result is generated in the table.  
The table shows the following information: Name , Combinational Area , Noncombinational Area , Buf/Inv Area , Nets with Violations , Max Trans Violations , Max Cap Violations , Dynamic Power , Leakage Power , WNS , and TNS .  
<!-- image -->

## Monitoring Computations in Job Monitor  
For multiple splits being created and computed on concurrently, each job submission are named, inspected, and managed from Job Monitor. Job Monitor is opened by choosing Tools > Job Monitor . DTCO jobs are organized under the DTCO category and the library names are listed under subcategories.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->

## Design Reviews  
The Custom Compiler design review system allows you to review design schematics and layouts, provide feedback, respond to feedback, and track review status. The built-in system enables collaborations between design and layout teams.  
This chapter contains the following topics:  
- About the Design Review System
- Workflows for Design Reviews
- Setting Up Design Review Policies
- Setting Up Automatic Review Notifications
- Creating, Editing, and Managing Design Reviews
- Opening an Existing Review
- Exporting Reviews
- Review Assistant Reference

## About the Design Review System  
The Custom Compiler design review system consists of the Review Assistant and the Review Manager. The Review Assistant lets you enter and respond to feedback. The Review Manager lets you browse the design libraries and locate existing reviews of interest.  
This topic describes the following:  
- Review Assistant
- Review Manager
- Review Data Structure  
<!-- image -->  
- Review Database
- Review Process

## Review Assistant  
The Review Assistant is the graphical user interface that lets you create and edit reviews.  
You use the Review assistant to:  
- Start, end, or delete reviews while in the Schematic Editor, Symbolic Editor, or Layout Editor.
- Enter review feedback without editing the design. The feedback can consist of text, annotations, and marked screen captures.
- Respond to the review feedback.
- Modify and track the status of the review feedback.  
The Review Assistant supports entering and viewing comments in languages, including Chinese, Korean, and Japanese. To enable this support, start the ibus-setup executable on your computer and follow the instructions.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
Review comments created on different hierarchy levels of the design can all be accessed from the Review Assistant.  
<!-- image -->  
- The Review Assistant displays the hierarchy levels up to the Stop Level .
- To facilitate design reviews, the review comments in the assistant are synchronized with the annotations in the design. When reviewing layouts, double-clicking the level\_n review item in the assistant descends in place. When reviewing schematics, doubleclicking the level \_n review item descends to level\_n.  
In the schematic example shown, double-cilcking the Level 2 annotation in the assistant descends to design level 2 and displays the annotations on the canvas.  
- If reviews on different hierarchy levels have the same name, the assistant displays the review name and merges the annotations from both levels.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->

## Review Manager  
The Review Manager is the graphical user interface that lets you search for reviews of interest.  
You use the Review Manager to:  
- Search for review of interest among design libraries. Available filters let you narrow the search.
- Browse the list of existing reviews for selected designs.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->

## Review Data Structure  
The Custom Compiler design review consists of reviews, issues, and annotations. Understanding the structure helps you determine how you set up the review policies and how to organize the reviews.  
In the Custom Compiler environment, a design can have multiple reviews. Each review has a description, an associated severity, and multiple issues.  
An issue can consist of a set of annotations or an image. When you create an issue, the canvas state and the set of annotations or images are preserved.  
<!-- image -->  
All review items are stored in a review database and are accessed using the Review Assistant.  
<!-- image -->

## Review Database  
The design review data is stored in a review database that is closely associated with the corresponding design. Understand the review database and its relationship with the design can help you quickly navigate and locate reviews of interest.  
The review database stores a set of reviews for a given cellview (schematic, symbol, or layout), and is automatically generated when you initiate a review for the cellview. The review database is also a cellview with a hierarchical OpenAccess (OA) database for storage. The review cellview exists in the same oaCell as the cellview that is reviewed.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
For easy identification of the review cellview, it has the same name as the reviewed cellview with an appended suffix (Tcl preference: dcReviewCellViewSuffix ). The default suffix is .review . For example, the review cellview for lib1/cell1/layout is lib1/cell1/ layout.review .

## Review Process  
The Custom Compiler design review process is based on the Review Data Structure.  
The following figure shows a simplified design review process that uses the Review Assistant. A reviewer initiates the review process (opens the review database for write operations), creates one or more review items, and adds one or more issues (each with annotations and screen shots) for each review item. See Review Data Structure.  
The reviewer then ends the review process, that is, saves and changes the review database to a read mode.  
<!-- image -->  
The review assignee then views the review items and examines each issue. The assignee can add comments to each review item and issue, and view the already existing comments. Each review item can then be marked approved, waived, fixed, or closed to conclude the specific review item.

## See Also  
- Workflows for Design Reviews

## Workflows for Design Reviews  
The design review process consists of two main tasks: setting up and maintaining reviews, and conducting reviews.  
This topic provides the following:  
- Workflow for Setting Up Design Reviews
- Workflow for Conducting Reviews

metadata.Header 2: Workflow for Setting Up Design Reviews

content:
## Workflow for Setting Up Design Reviews  
Before design reviews can be started, administrators should set up design review policies to define review users and permissions. In addition, if you can optionally set up automatic email notification so that members and approvers are aware of new or modified reviews.  
The following table shows the workflow steps for setting up the design reviews.  
|   Step |                                                        | See...                                    |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
|      1 | Set up the design review policy for your organization. | Setting Up Design Review Policies         |
|      2 | (Optional) Set up automatic review notifications.      | Setting Up Automatic Review Notifications |

## Workflow for Conducting Reviews  
You use the Review Assistant to conduct reviews. The following table shows the workflow steps for design reviews.  
<!-- image -->  
The Review Assistant in the Custom Compiler environment is designed to facilitate the design review process. The Review Assistant lets you provide comments about layouts, respond to feedback, and track review status.  
This video tutorial shows how to start reviews, create and edit a review, add annotations in a review, add and reply to comments, and export the review data using the Review Assistant.  
| Step             | See...          |
|------------------|-----------------|
| 1 Open a design. | Opening Designs |  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
|   Step |                                    | See...                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------|------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|      2 | Display the Review Assistant.      | Displaying the Review Assistant                                                                                                                                                                 |
|      3 | Start a review session.            | Starting Design Review Sessions                                                                                                                                                                 |
|      4 | Create and edit a review.          | • Creating New Reviews • Editing Reviews                                                                                                                                                        |
|      5 | Mark up the design.                | • Adding Annotations in a Review • Editing, Moving, and Deleting Annotations • Adding Images to a Review • Displaying Annotations and Images • Hiding Annotations • Deleting Issues and Reviews |
|      6 | Start or reply to discussions.     | Adding and Replying to Discussion Comments                                                                                                                                                      |
|      7 | End the review session.            | Ending Design Review Sessions                                                                                                                                                                   |
|      8 | (Optional) Export the review data. | Exporting Reviews                                                                                                                                                                               |  
After reviews are created, you can search for and open existing reviews. You use the Review Manager to search for existing reviews. See Opening an Existing Review.

## See Also  
- About the Design Review System
- Review Assistant Reference

## Setting Up Design Review Policies  
Design review policies enforce rules implemented by your organization. The policies define users and their permission levels for various design review activities.  
This topic describes the following:  
- About Design Review Policies
- Default Design Review Policy
- Creating Design Review Policies
- Modify Existing Design Review Policies

## About Design Review Policies  
A design review policy defines review users and review permissions as follows:  
| Policy Component   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Users              | Review users can be one of the following: • Creator: Creates the review. • Assignee: Is assigned an issue. • Member: Is a participant in the review. • Approver: Approves the proposed modifications.                                                                                                             |
| Permissions        | Review users can have permission to: • Create issues, add review annotations in the design, and add images in the review comments. • Modify issues, review annotations in the design, and images in the review description. • Delete issues, review annotations in the design, and images in the review comments. |

## Default Design Review Policy  
A default design review policy is provided, but it is not activated. The policy is defined as follows:  
| Operation   | Description                                                                                                 |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Create      | Review users can create issues, add review annotations in the design, or add images in the review comments. |
| Modify      | Review users can modify issues, review annotations in the design, or images in the review comments.         |  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
| Operation   | Description                                                                                                         |
|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Delete      | Review users can delete reviews or issues within a review. Review users cannot delete review annotations or images. |  
To activate the default design review policy, run the dc::setPolicy Tcl command as follows:  
dc::setPolicy default

## Creating Design Review Policies  
You can create your own design review policies for your organization. To create a new set of design review policies, use the dc::addPolicy Tcl command.

## Modify Existing Design Review Policies  
To modify an existing design review policy, use the dc::addPolicy Tcl command to overwrite the existing policy. For example, to modify the default design review policy, you can use the dc::addPolicy command as follows:  
```
dc::addPolicy default -canCreateProcnewCanCreate -canDeleteProcnewCanDelete -canModifyProcnewCanModify
```

## Setting Up Automatic Review Notifications  
Design review members and approvers can be notified of any new or modified review input. This topic describes how to set up automatic notifications.  
To set up the automatic review notification:  
1. Create a Tcl procedure for sending email notifications.  
In the Tcl procedure:  
- Use the sendmail Linux command, or an equivalent method for email transfers.
- Include to , subject , and body variables.

## Examples:  
```
proc sendmail {to subject body} proc custom_notification {to subject body}
```  
<!-- image -->  
2. Set the dcReviewNotificationProc Tcl preference to specify the procedure you created in step 1.  
For example:  
```
db::setPrefValue dcReviewNotificationProc -value send_email_proc
```  
3. When you create reviews, make sure you define the Approver(s) and Member(s) in the Create Review dialog box.  
Only the defined approvers and members receive email notifications. Email notifications are automatically sent when you end reviews.

## See Also  
- Creating New Reviews
- Editing Reviews
- Ending Design Review Sessions

metadata.Header 2: Creating, Editing, and Managing Design Reviews

content:
## Creating, Editing, and Managing Design Reviews  
You use the Review Assistant to create new reviews, enter and respond to design review feedback, track review status, and end reviews in the Schematic Editor, Symbolic Editor, and Layout Editor.  
This section describes the following:  
- Displaying the Review Assistant
- Starting Design Review Sessions
- Creating New Reviews
- Copying Reviews
- Editing Reviews
- Adding Annotations in a Review
- Editing, Moving, and Deleting Annotations
- Adding Images to a Review
- Displaying Annotations and Images
- Hiding Annotations
- Deleting Issues and Reviews  
- Adding and Replying to Discussion Comments
- Ending Design Review Sessions  
<!-- image -->  
Review Assistant facilitates design reviews by allowing you to create, edit, and manage reviews, add annotations and images, track review statuses, and collaborate through discussions. It supports hierarchical navigation, synchronization with design annotations, and exporting reviews to HTML for external sharing.

## [Displaying the Review Assistant](https://spdocs.synopsys.com/dow_retrieve/latest/training/dg/custom_compiler/CC_design_review_assistant.mp4)  
You can display the Review Assistant in the Schematic Editor, Symbolic Editor, or Layout Editor.  
To display the Review assistant:  
- In the Schematic Editor, Symbolic Editor, or Layout Editor, choose Window > Assistants > Review Assistant .  
The assistant appears on the left side of the design editor tab and lists existing reviews, if any.  
The following diagram shows the components of the Review Assistant. For the quick reference, see Review Assistant Reference.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->

## See Also  
- About the Design Review System
- Creating, Editing, and Managing Design Reviews
- Opening an Existing Review

## Starting Design Review Sessions  
Starting design reviews in the Review Assistant enables functions that permit you to add and edit reviews and issues.  
To start a design review:  
- On the Review Assistant toolbar, click Start Review .  
<!-- image -->  
As soon as you start a review, a review cellview (.review) is automatically generated.

## Creating New Reviews  
To create a review for a design:  
1. On the Review Assistant toolbar, click New Review .  
<!-- image -->  
The Create Review dialog box opens.  
<!-- image -->  
2. In the Description box:
- a. Type the review title on the first line. The title appears in the Title column in the Review Assistant.
- b. Type a description for the review on subsequent lines. The description appears in the Description section of the Review Assistant.  
<!-- image -->  
3. Choose the Severity of the review comments:
4. Specify the Assignee , the recipient of the review.
5. Specify the list of review Approver(s) , users who can set the review as Approved , Closed , or Waived .
4. Type the space-separated list of user names in the Approver(s) box. Alternatively, click , and select the user names.  
| Argument    | Description                                      |
|-------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Enhancement | New features to be added to the existing design. |
| Critical    | Defects that must be fixed.                      |
| Information | Notes to the designers or team.                  |  
<!-- image -->  
You must define approvers if you want approvers and review members to automatically receive notifications when you add or modify reviews.  
6. Specify the review Member(s) , users who are notified of the review but are not required to approve.  
<!-- image -->  
Type the space-separated list of user names in the Member(s) box. Alternatively, click , and select the user names.  
You must define members if you want approvers and review members to automatically receive notifications when you add or modify reviews.

## See Also  
- Setting Up Automatic Review Notifications
- Adding Annotations in a Review
- Editing Reviews

## Copying Reviews  
After you add a design review, you can copy the same review.  
<!-- image -->

## To copy a review:  
1. In the Review Assistant, select the review, and click Copy Review .
2. To add one or more library, cell, views to for review, click Add in the Destination section. The Add View dialog box opens.
3. Enter the Library, Cell, View and click OK or Apply .  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
The library, cell, view appears in the Destination section in the Copy Review dialog box.  
4. (Optional) To delete a destination from a library, cell, view from the Destination section, select the library, cell, view and click Remove .
5. The description of the copied design review appears in the Description box. You can edit the description, if needed.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
6. Select the Include Issues box to copy the design review annotations associated with the review. By default, this box is not selected.
7. Click OK or Apply. The copied review appears in the Review Assistant table.

## Cloning Reviews  
You can clone an existing design review from the Review Assistant. The cloned review contains the same information as the reference review.  
To clone a review:  
1. In the table right-click on the Title of the review, and select the Clone Review option.
2. The cloned review appears in the first row of the table.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->

## See Also  
- Creating New Reviews
- Editing Reviews
- Deleting Issues and Reviews

## Editing Reviews  
After you add a review, you can edit it to set the review status or change the original review information, such as the title, description, assignee, or approvers.  
To edit a review:  
1. In the Review Assistant, select the review, and click Edit Review .  
<!-- image -->  
The Edit Review dialog box opens.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
2. Choose the review Status to indicate the current state of the selected review:
3. Set or modify the remaining options as described in Creating New Reviews.  
| Argument   | Description                                                |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| Open       | The review is in progress.                                 |
| Approved   | The review is finished and all issues have been addressed. |
| Fixed      | The review issues have been fixed.                         |
| Waived     | The review is no longer applicable or under consideration. |
| Closed     | Reviewers should no longer view or add issues or comments. |

## See Also  
- Adding Annotations in a Review
- Editing, Moving, and Deleting Annotations
- Ending Design Review Sessions

## Adding Annotations in a Review  
You can add annotations in the design to let designers know the locations of issues. Annotations include text callouts, arrows, ellipses, and so on. The annotations are overlays and do not alter the original design.  
When you add review annotations, you are creating issues that are stored as part of the review in the Review Assistant. Each issue can contain multiple annotations. Keep this organization in mind when you create review annotations.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
To add annotations in a review:  
1. In the Review Assistant, select the review.
2. On the Review Assistant toolbar, click Add Annotation .  
<!-- image -->  
The Add Review Annotation dialog box opens.  
<!-- image -->  
3. In the Description box:
- a. Type the issue title on the first line. The title appears in the Title column in the Review Assistant.
- b. Type a description for the issue on subsequent lines. The description appears in the Description section of the Review Assistant.
4. Select the Type of annotation you want to add.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
| Argument          | Description   |
|-------------------|---------------|
| Callout Object    |               |
| Callout Highlight |               |  
5. In the Options section, set the following as applicable:
6. On the canvas, add the selected annotation: Click the starting and ending points for the annotation.  
| Setting Option   | Description                                                          |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Color            | Color of the annotation objects.                                     |
| Angle            | Angle of the Wire annotation: Orthogonal , Diagonal , or Any Angle . |
| Width            | Width of the Wire annotation.                                        |
| Text             | Text to use for the Callout annotation type.                         |  
For ellipses, the starting point is the center of the ellipse.  
7. To add more annotations, repeat steps 4 through 6.
8. When you are finished, click OK in the dialog box.

## See Also  
- Editing, Moving, and Deleting Annotations
- Adding Images to a Review

## Editing, Moving, and Deleting Annotations  
You can edit, move and delete design review annotations from the Review Assistant:  
<!-- image -->  
- Editing Annotations
- Moving Annotations
- Deleting Annotations

## Editing Annotations  
To edit the design review annotations:  
1. Select the issue, and select the Edit Issue ( ) option.  
<!-- image -->  
The Edit Review Annotation dialog box opens.  
<!-- image -->  
2. Modify any of the settings. For the descriptions of the options, see Adding Annotations in a Review.  
<!-- image -->

## Moving Annotations  
You can move design review annotations on the canvas. To move one or more annotations:  
1. On the canvas, select the annotations you want to move. You can area-select multiple annotations.
2. Perform any one of the following:
- Select the Move Annotation ( ) option.
- Press the following keys in the keyboard:
- For schematic designs, press Shift+m
- For layout designs, press m
- Enter the idc::move command in the console.
3. In the canvas, drag the annotation to the new location.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->

## Deleting Annotations  
You can delete the design review annotations that are no longer needed. To delete one or more annotations:  
1. On the canvas, select the annotations you want to delete. You can area-select multiple annotations.
2. Perform any one of the following:
- Select the Delete Annotation  
(  
<!-- image -->  
- Press the Delete key on the keyboard.
- Enter the idc::delete command in the console.

## Select annotation  
<!-- image -->

## See Also  
- Adding Annotations in a Review
- Displaying Annotations and Images
- Editing Reviews
- Adding Images to a Review

## Adding Images to a Review  
You can add a screen capture (image) of the canvas to your review to clarify your review comments.

## Annotation is deleted  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
When you add images, you are creating issues that are stored as part of the review in the Review Assistant. Each issue contains only one image.  
<!-- image -->  
To add an image to the review:  
1. In the Review Assistant, select the review or issue.
2. On the Review assistant toolbar, click Add Image ( ).
3. Specify the design region for the screen capture:
- To capture the entire viewport, click anywhere on the canvas.
- To capture a specific area, draw a rectangle around the area of interest on the canvas.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
The Add Image dialog box opens and displays the image you just captured.  
<!-- image -->  
4. If the image looks unsatisfactory and you want to retake the screen capture, click Recapture .  
The new image appears in the dialog box.  
5. In the Description box:
- a. Type the review title on the first line. The title appears in the Title column in the Review Assistant.
- b. Type a description for the review on subsequent lines. The description appears in the Description section of the Review Assistant.
6. In the Image Caption box, type a short summary of the image.
7. When you are finished, click OK .  
The new image (issue) appears in the Review Assistant.

## Displaying Annotations and Images  
If annotations and images are hidden or not visible on the canvas, you can use the Show Issue command to display them.  
To display annotations and images associated with an issue:  
- In the Review Assistant, do one of the following:
- Double-click the issue.
- Select the issue, and click Show Issue on the Review Assistant toolbar.  
<!-- image -->  
If you selected an issue that contains annotations, the annotations appear on the canvas.  
<!-- image -->  
If you selected an issue that contains an image, the Display Images dialog box opens.  
<!-- image -->

## Hiding Annotations  
You can hide annotations to view the design in its original state and add new annotations.  
<!-- image -->  
To hide existing annotations that are currently displayed on the canvas:  
1. In the Review Assistant, select the review.
2. On the Review Assistant toolbar, click Restore Window .  
<!-- image -->

## See Also  
- Displaying Annotations and Images

## Deleting Issues and Reviews  
You can delete reviews or issues that are no longer needed.  
To delete an issue or a review:  
1. In the Review Assistant, select the issue or review.
2. On the Review Assistant toolbar, click Delete Selected ( ). ×  
<!-- image -->

metadata.Header 2: Adding and Replying to Discussion Comments

content:
## Adding and Replying to Discussion Comments  
You can add or reply to comments during design reviews to help communicate questions or highlight issues for other reviewers to discuss.  
To add or reply to comments in a review:  
1. In the Review Assistant, locate the Discussion section and type your comments in the second text box.
2. Click Add comment to discussion .
3. View the comment you entered.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->

## Ending Design Review Sessions  
When you are finished creating reviews or issues, you can end the review session to save the changes. Ending the review session and saving the changes allow other reviewers to see your input. You can also discard all changes made during the current review session and end the review.  
This topic describes the two ways to end reviews:  
- Saving Changes and Ending Reviews
- Discarding All Changes and Ending Reviews

## Saving Changes and Ending Reviews  
To save all changes made and end the review session:  
- On the Review Assistant toolbar, click End Review .  
<!-- image -->  
The new reviews and issues you created during the review session are saved, and the session closes. If automatic review notification was set up, approvers and members are automatically notified by email.

## See Also  
- Setting Up Automatic Review Notifications

metadata.Header 2: Discarding All Changes and Ending Reviews

content:
## Discarding All Changes and Ending Reviews  
To discard all changes made during the current review session and end the session:  
- On the Review Assistant toolbar, click Discard Review .  
<!-- image -->  
All reviews and associated issues created during the current review session are discarded, and the session closes.

## Opening an Existing Review  
You use the Review Manager to locate an existing review or issue. After you locate it, you can open it in the Review Assistant.  
To open a review:  
1. In the Library Manager, double-click the design review cellview (.review).  
The Review Manager opens.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
2. In the Search Assistant area, click Search Type , and choose one of the following:  
<!-- image -->

## 3. Set the search criteria:  
- If you selected the Library search type, select the design library, and optionally specify the additional filters.
- If you selected the Design Hierarchy search type, specify the Library , Cell , and View names, and optionally specify the additional filters.

## Library  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
4. Click Search  
.  
The list of reviews appears.  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
5. To further filter the results, click View and choose a command.  
<!-- image -->  
6. To open a review or issue, double-click the review name or issue name.  
The review or issue opens in the Review Assistant.

## Exporting Reviews  
You can export specified reviews to an HTML file to view the design review information without having to run the Custom Compiler tool.

## To export reviews:  
1. Open the review that you want to export using the Review Manager. See Opening an Existing Review.
2. On the Search Assistant toolbar, click Export Review .  
<!-- image -->  
<!-- image -->  
The Export Design Review to HTML dialog box opens.  
<!-- image -->  
3. In the Output File box, specify the directory and name for the exported file. If you do not specify a directory, the review data is exported to <current\_working\_directory>/ synopsys\_custom/reports.
4. Select Export Images to export the corresponding images from the review.
5. Select Open in Tab to open the HTML file containing the exported review data in a new tab in the Custom Compiler window.
6. Click OK .  
The review data is exported to an HTML file in the default output file directory or in the directory you specified. If you selected Open in Tab, the HTML file opens immediately in a separate tab in the Custom Compiler window.
